mechanism: A Cloudflare Pages project with Pages Functions, behind Access for the owner's email
only. While the page is open it calls the function every 60 seconds per connected project; the
function holds a read-only fine-grained GitHub token, makes conditional GitHub REST reads and hands
the raw records back; the page parses them and shows what waits on the owner. The owner answers
cards and records plans through prefilled GitHub new-file links that the owner commits, so the desk
holds no write credential.
problem: The owner runs several AI-built projects that stop whenever they need a ruling. Today the owner
learns of waits from a read-only page rebuilt hourly (Operations-Hub, no longer in use) or by
scrolling Claude Code sessions, so waits are missed or slow and "quiet" can't be trusted
(PROJECT.md §2, Part 2 "requests get buried"). Only the owner is affected.
milestones: M1, M2, M2B, MD1, MD2, MD3, M3A, M3B, M3C

**How this spec is used (owner's ruling of 2026-10-06, decisions/questions/P-001-build-path.md,
question 0).** P-001's automated pipeline closed with `re-scope` (decisions/P-001/stop-6.md). The
owner chose to build the desk outside the pipeline, from the approved brief and this spec, in three
milestones (as ruled then; the owner's design-step ruling of 2026-10-07 added a fourth, MD, below). Each piece is checked by the Reviewer and merged by the owner; there is no further
Critic gate, and the experiments run during Build. This spec stays `status: draft`: it is the
Builder's working brief, not a frozen spec (see Risks, "No freeze").

  model v3.4.0 on 2026-10-17 (L-0015). For a body in S-032's form, its forms read as its draft 1
  of 2026-10-16 (7108d1d) did, so the desk's readers do not change. AC61's list "Where the desk
  differs from S-032" is rewritten so it is true now:
  - the item saying S-032's J2 leaves a merged pull request untied when the plan's `· sprints:`
    names it is gone: S-032's J2 now ties it through the plan, as AC60 does;
  - the named display leniencies stay;

    round 1 of the desk follow-ups, B1);

    no change to the desk (reviews/S-032/_build-review-round1-verbatim.md in
    Personal-Org-Operating-Model, N1 and N2).
- **2. The merge-commit message.** Since 2026-10-17 the repository's merge setting is "Pull
  request title and description" (docs/SETUP.md step 5; L-0015). A merge commit's first line is
  now `<pull request title> (#<n>)` and its body is the pull request's description, for example
  e9630a4, "Model 3.4.0: … (#79)". It no longer begins `Merge pull request #<n>`. The deploy
  workflow put the whole merge message in a push run's title, so that title would now hold the
  pull request's whole description, and the Queue's Deploys row shows a run's title. GitHub's
  expressions cannot take a message's first line. So the smallest honest fix is this:
  - **from Setup CS14** (the Chief of Staff's), a push run's title is `deploy <sha>` alone;
  - a hand-started run keeps `deploy <sha> — <note>`;
  - the pull request a push deploy carries is named by AC72's "Matches PR #<n>'s merge" line,
    from the records, not from the title.

  AC72's parse holds for both title forms. No desk code changes for it, only AC72's test (AC72;
  "Toolchain and deploy route", Workflow 2).
- **3. J12's retries back off.** Retrying a failed J12 read on every cycle could double a
  project's function calls. With five failing projects, that breaks AC14's margin of 10,000 a
  day. Now a failed J12 read waits 5, 10, 20 and 40 minutes after failures in a row, then 60
  minutes each time, until a read answers; an answer sets it back to the start. A rate limit
  keeps its plain 60-minute wait. AC14 gains the case of J12 failing all day, at 5,715 calls at
  most (A3). The Builder tests it with the scheduler's fake clock (J12, AC14).
- **Changed in place:** AC14, AC61 and AC72; J12; A3; Workflow 2's run title; the S-032 lines
  in "What this spec does not cover" and AC66; Setup CS14 (new); a fact under "Facts relied on";
  Areas touched's note; and the brief.

**Where the build stands (amendment of 2026-10-17, model 3.5.0's records; draft 8).**

What this leaves undone, and what it still won't show you: your Chief of Staff's own token use
and cost stay "not recorded", because no tool lets a conversation read its own figures. Each small pull
request that the automatic job merges for you (a filed question, an answer the Chief of Staff
records, a tidy-up, or a note of the Chief of Staff's work) still shows on the desk as waiting on
you while it is open, so the desk stops reading quiet, usually for minutes before the job merges
it, or for hours on the runs where the job has to wait for its timer and GitHub starts it late:
you chose to keep that "waiting on you" while they are open, and to take them off the Timeline
once merged, unless the plan lists one. No real milestone will read "reached" when this lands: first the new reader
goes live, after you merge it and approve its preview, and only then is your first milestone
marked reached from your acceptance of it, and you are asked about the answering and usage
milestones through filed questions. An answer you give through the answer link on the desk you use
today won't carry its milestone, so once the Chief of Staff tidies that question away, its ruling
no longer links to the milestone; answers from the trial view's answer box carry it. A piece of
the Chief of Staff's work with no recorded end stops reading "working" after 8 hours. Five other
records the screens wait for are still not kept, and, as you chose, the agents' usage list
stays as it is. What you will see change, in the trial view only (the views you
accepted stay exactly as they are): each question and decision card names the milestone it
unblocks and lists its facts with their sources; your Chief of Staff's tile, running log and
working-now sheet show its recorded work, and who has the ball names it while it works; a
milestone you accept shows as reached, with its date; the automatic job's merged pull requests
no longer show as work on the Timeline, unless the plan lists one, while the questions and answers they carry still show in
your Queue and in "Done today"; and the answer box fills in the question's milestone line for
you. Nothing here is irreversible: it changes the plan only, and each choice
can be changed again.

- **Why now.** From the audit of 2026-10-16 you picked "File every ask (Recommended)", whose
  option text ends "Without this the new screens stay mostly "not recorded""
  (decisions/questions/P-001-trial-view-notes-2.md:165-166). The model change is done: model
  S-033 (Personal-Org-Operating-Model specs/S-033-file-every-ask.md, frozen, merged at 90f53e3,
  its PR #35), adopted here with model v3.5.0 in PR #81 (ledger L-0016). The record this revision
  rests on is L-0016's `licenses_next:` (docs/LEDGER.md:227): "S-001's next revision has the desk
  read the new records (open questions with their milestone and context, the Chief of Staff's
  sessions, a milestone's reached mark) and accept the reached part before any line carries one;
  only then is M1 marked reached from its acceptance record, and the owner is asked about M2 and
  M2B through filed questions." In the session on 2026-10-17 you wrote "Go ahead and", the
  message ending there, and in your next message "Ignore and *", which the session read as "Go
  ahead" alone; the session then started this revision. Those two messages are in the session
  only, not in a ruling record.
- **What the desk now reads, each where it showed "not recorded"** (no new screen, and no new
  kind of request: every record is a blob in the tree the desk already reads):
  1. **The milestone and the facts behind each ask.** A question file now names the milestone

**Notifications the moment anything waits on you (amendment of 2026-10-18; draft 9).**

Draft 9 follows the first review of the built code, which failed on defects now being fixed: a
question you had already answered could still be notified if its answer merged during a run; an
item held back while your phone's subscription was gone could be dropped after one "try later";
and the desk's check before an answer link, and its usage bar after a cost notification, could be
out of date. The spec now says exactly what the fixed code does; nothing new is asked of you.
Draft 6 failed its first check on two points, both now fixed: the warning issue that tells you
the sender has stopped could have been kept shut by a file that a branch or a stranger's pull
request saved, and the desk's half of the new "closed without merging" check was not pinned
down. Drafts 6 and 7 change three things for you. If the pull request that records your answer to
a question is closed without being merged, the question comes back to you, on the desk and on your
phone, with one notification; in a few rare cases the desk can lag behind your phone while it
stays open on your screen, and it catches up when you tap the notification or come back to the
desk. If the sender cannot tell how long it has been unable to read its own memory, it opens its
warning issue to you at once rather than staying silent, so a passing GitHub failure can open one;
it closes itself at the sender's next good run. The desk and the sender each make a few more small
reads of GitHub to do this. The rest writes down choices made while the sender was built, such as
the exact words of the notification you get when notifications first come on. Draft 4 failed one
check: the test meant
to prove the fix for the stale link you reported used your real question, which was filed before the
mark that holds it existed, so the test could not pass.
It now adds that one mark to a copy of the question, and keeps the unmarked real question as a
second case. A research check also failed on one point that matters to you: GitHub's own
documentation says its usage reports for a personal account may apply only to someone who has
bought their own Copilot plan, so GitHub may report no Actions use to the desk for your account.
If so, the desk says so in plain words, shows no bar and sends no $50 notifications, and you rely
on GitHub's own e-mails at 90% and 100% of your included minutes, which I then recommend you turn
on; the first test call settles it. Even if it works, at today's price a $50 step needs about 8,300
charged minutes in one month, so at the rate seen so far you may get no $50 notification at all,
though the bar shows the estimate. Some limits remain. Notifications cover only what a record
shows: "verdicts to write" never notifies, a held loop notifies only an hour after a check went
red, and nothing outside the records notifies. If a sender cannot run at all, nothing on your phone
says so. If only a cost notification finds that your phone's subscription has lapsed, the warning
issue waits until something else is sent, so your costs stay out of public view. The senders run
unattended with your notification secrets, so anything that reaches main,
including an agent's push made under your account, could misuse them; at worst it could copy your
notification keys out, and anyone could then send your phone notifications until you make new keys
and turn notifications on again; it could also copy the new usage token, which, if GitHub accepts
the narrow kind I ask for, shows only your Actions use and cost, and if only the older kind works,
can reach more of your account. You check those settings at each milestone. The operating-model
project's fast path costs money: your account is past its 3,000 included minutes this month and has
a card on file, so its minutes are charged, about 530 a month by my estimate, roughly $3 a month,
cut from about 730; Service-Desk's own sender is free. Most of the account's use seems to come from
that project's existing checks, which this plan does not change. As you asked, nothing about cost
needs your approval: where GitHub reports it, the desk shows this month's Actions minutes as a
share of your included 3,000, then an estimated cost so far once past them, and your phone gets one
notification each time that estimate passes another $50. Something the operating-model project's
events miss can take up to about three hours to notify. A question your Chief of Staff asks in a
session without marking it, or one still open eight hours later, shows its answer link as before.
This work comes before the rest of the trial view, so your launch date of 11 November is at risk;
it needs about two and a half hours of your time. What changes for you: a deploy waiting for your
approval counts as waiting on you on the desk now, as you answered, which changes your 16 October
ruling for Service-Desk. Whenever anything moves from the agents to you, your iPhone shows one
notification, usually within a few minutes, naming the project and what waits, and a tap opens it
on the desk. A question being asked in your session, or answered there while its record is on its
way, shows as such, with no answer link and no notification. Your one-time setup is about 50
minutes, in a set order, including one new token for your billing use that you renew when it
expires, and part of it is repeated at launch. Nothing here is irreversible: a switch in each
project stops its sender, and notifications can be turned off on the phone.

- **How the new request changes the 8 October ruling, read here** (C). The trigger widens from
  "when it raises a card" to anything that waits, now. Web Push to the desk on the Home Screen,
  sent from GitHub, the subscription a GitHub secret the owner sets, no database and no new
  Cloudflare service, all stand. The sender is each project's own GitHub workflow, not the
  Orchestrator's card step, which sees only Service-Desk's cards; that follow-up of the ruling is
  not taken up, and the Orchestrator is not changed.
- **The fast path: the safest route, and its full cost** (C, as the fast-path ruling asks).
  - **The route:** the operating-model project sends its own notifications from a workflow in its
    own repository (Workflow 4), reading only its own records with its own workflow token, with
    the notification secrets set there by the owner. No token crosses projects. It runs
    Service-Desk's public sender code at one pinned commit, checked to be on Service-Desk's main
    before it runs; a sender change reaches it only through a reviewed pull request there that
    moves the pin and reads the change between the two pins.
  - **The minutes, and what they cost** (stated as information; the owner's cost instruction sets
    no approval step): GitHub Pro includes 3,000 Actions minutes a month for the whole account,
    shared by every private repository the owner has; public repositories use none; each job is
    rounded up to a whole minute (GitHub's billing documentation, Facts relied on). The account has
    a card on file and was already past the 3,000 in October (the owner's billing answer), so every
    Workflow 4 minute is charged: standard Linux runners cost $0.006 a minute from 2026-01-01
    (research Q-015 F4.1, A; its source check passes the prices). Workflow 4's runs are cut as far as safety
    allows (below), to about 530 minutes a month (E), about $3.20 a month; about 750 minutes,
    about $4.50, if a skipped job does not start a `workflow_run` (C, EXP-006 case 9); draft 3's
    triggers came to about 730, about $4.40. The desk shows the account's whole use and its cost
    (AC78), and GitHub can e-mail at 90% and 100% of the included use (Setup N11). EXP-006 records
    a week's real figure.
  - **Outside this spec's scope, said plainly:** the operating-model project's existing `ci`
    workflow appears to be most of the account's use, about 4,100 minutes from 1 to 17 October by
    its runs' times (plan review round 3, N1; C, the billing figures were not read). This spec
    neither changes nor counts on changing it; reducing it is that project's own work, and the
    desk's bar (AC78) shows its effect.
  - **The delays there:** its pushes to main that touch `questions/`, and a no-secret workflow
    that runs when a pull request is opened, reopened or marked ready, each start its sender within
    a few minutes, about as fast as Service-Desk's. Something an event misses waits for the
    3-hourly check: up to about 3 hours, worse if GitHub runs the schedule late.
  - **The secrets twice:** the same VAPID key pair, contact and subscription are set in both
    projects (a second state key differs), so a leak in either touches both, and turning
    notifications on again means updating both.
  - **Compared, a cross-project token (not chosen):** for that project to start Service-Desk's
    sender, a token held there would need write power on Service-Desk: Contents write for
    `repository_dispatch` (Q-011 T10b), which can push to Service-Desk's unprotected main, or
    Actions write for `workflow_dispatch`, which can also start, cancel and delete runs and their
    artifacts. Service-Desk's sender would also need a read token for the private project, and
    its public logs and state would carry that project's items.
- **No model change is needed.** The senders use the desk's own reader, not the model's
  owner-signal job, which posts only two commit statuses (owner_signal.py:1-30). The asks-merge

**Notifications open your page (amendment of 2026-10-19).**

Notifications went live on the older view of the desk, as you chose; this follow-up makes the desk's
Home Screen icon and every notification tap open your page, the new design, instead. The older view
still opens at the plain address for anyone who goes there. An icon you added before this change
may keep opening the older view until you remove it and add it again; taps open your page either
way. Adding it again may give your phone a new notification value, which you then paste into GitHub
once more (about 5 minutes; Setup N13). When the new design becomes the desk itself (MD3), the icon
and taps go back to the plain address. Nothing here is irreversible, and what notifies does not
change.

- **The ruling** (decisions/questions/P-001-notify-which-view.md, pull request #119): "A. Go live
  now, switch later (Recommended)": "Turn notifications on today with the older view; then make the
  icon and taps open the new design as a quick follow-up."
- **Changed in place:** AC74's tap (with J17's addresses), AC75's manifest and service worker,
  their tests, Setup N13 (new), EXP-006 case 12, the brief's step 6.
- **When MD3 or M3 makes the new design the desk** (C): the `?sandbox` flag goes; `start_url`
  returns to `/` (`id` stays `/`, so the app is the same one), the sender's tap addresses to
  `/?open=<key>` and `/`; and a `?sandbox` address, from an old icon or an old notification, opens
  `/` with its other parameters kept, so nothing on the phone breaks. That pull request carries it.

**Work ahead by milestones (amendment of 2026-10-18; draft 6).**

The first check of the build failed, on a mistake in the build that the Builder is fixing, and
raised three points that draft 6 settles. When the plan you just recorded lands, your draft now
clears quietly; "A newer plan was recorded; your draft was set aside" shows only when that plan's
order differs from your draft's. Before you move anything, the screen says "No changes yet", not
that your changes are on this phone. And "Record plan" stays off until your milestones are read, so
it can never record an empty plan over yours. Draft 6 also names some words on the screen that the
mockup does not draw, and reads an impossible date in an estimate, such as 30 February, as a line
that can't be read.

Draft 4 passed both checks, with notes that draft 5 folds in: chiefly, if GitHub ever refuses to say
which files a pull request changed, the Timeline now shows every pull request rather than hiding
most of them, so at worst an estimate shows there. Draft 3 failed both of its checks again, on small
points that draft 4 fixes: the build's instructions still told it to copy your private project's
files, which they no longer do; the summary said estimates show nowhere on the Timeline when they
would have, so now a Timeline rule keeps them off it; and a settings rule would have failed on your
operating-model project's "planning off" entry. Draft 2 failed both of its checks too, and draft 3
fixed them. The rough finish broke the day after an estimate of "no work left", so the screen would
have gone blank most days; such an estimate now holds until you accept the milestone. A test banned
words that your own milestone names use, and another would have copied your private project's files
into this public repository; neither does now. Some things are left undone or wait on you. No rough
estimate exists yet: your Chief of Staff makes the first one for each milestone once this lands, and
until then each milestone reads "not made yet" and shows no rough finish. Each new estimate waits
for you to merge it and sends your phone a notification while it waits; once merged it shows nowhere
on the Timeline, and Work ahead shows the last one you merged. That lasts until a small
operating-model change, reviewed in that project, lets the automatic job merge estimates too, as you
ruled on 19 October. Several things differ from the mockup you approved. The design milestones'
"work done · accept?" is not built, because no record says a milestone's work is done: MD1 and MD2
read "work filed" with their sprints, and "once you accept it" when your Chief of Staff estimates no
work left. The launch-target line is not built. "Phone notifications" is not under "Not milestones
yet", because notifications are built and live. A tap there asks for the milestone, and your Chief
of Staff files the question at its next session, not at once. The "Work ahead" button on Home, a
dropped-milestones fold and some other words on the screen are not in the mockup; your Chief of
Staff shows you the button before the build. What you will see: a "Work ahead" button on Home opens
your milestones not yet reached, in the order you set, with the reached ones folded away; each shows
where it stands, your Chief of Staff's latest rough estimate, and a rough finish, a range of dates
added up in your order from today, labelled an expectation, never a deadline. You move milestones up
and down and tap "Record plan" to commit your order, with no dates in it, as you answer cards today.
Your audit picks that aren't milestones yet sit under "Not milestones yet": a tap asks for one to be
added, your Chief of Staff files the question, and adding it still needs your approval. The
operating-model project shows its open sprint: the records say it has one, though the mockup said
none. The full list of differences is below. As you ruled on 19 October, it is built now in the
trial view, where you try it on the preview first and accept it as its own milestone; it becomes
part of the desk when you accept the chosen design. Nothing here is irreversible: it changes the
plan only, and each choice can be changed again.

**The automatic job's pull requests, being recorded (amendment of 2026-10-19; draft 7).**

Both checks of the build passed their third round, and draft 7 only writes down two of their notes;
nothing new is built. First, a rare, short gap: if your phone's sender can't download a job log it
needs while a pull request has waited unjudged for over 45 minutes, your phone can be told about it
a little before the desk stops showing "Being recorded"; it clears at the sender's next good read.
Second, a small extra safeguard for later: the desk trusts the job's permission line today because
the job always prints it first; a later change would make the desk check that order itself. The
security check found no way, today, to fake that line.

Draft 6: both checks of the build passed on their second round, with notes, and draft 6 records the
Orchestrator's rulings on four of them. The security check found one way the forged log could still
fool your phone and the desk: a job run that stops right after the planted line. Now the desk and
your phone believe only a job run that finished cleanly; any other finish counts as forged, and
every pull request it names waits on you until a clean run judges it. The fix that removes the
cause, in the operating model, is still to come. Two smaller gaps close too: if the job never gets
round to a pull request whose checks are done, it waits on you after 45 minutes rather than showing
"Being recorded" for ever; and your phone no longer ignores a real job run for a minute or two just
after the default branch moves, which could have told you of a pull request the desk still showed as
being recorded. The two shared files are now owner-approval paths, as planned.

Draft 5: both checks of the build failed in round 1, and draft 5 recorded the Orchestrator's rulings
on what they found.
The security check found that anyone who can push a branch here could give a file a name that makes
the automatic job's log seem to say another pull request was merged, so neither your phone nor the
desk would show it waiting on you. Now a log that names a pull request twice, or out of order,
counts as saying nothing, and every pull request it names waits on you until a clean run judges it.
Changing the job so it never prints such a name raw belongs to the operating model, not to this
work. The desk check found that the desk could keep showing "Being recorded" after the record behind
the job's permission was deleted; the desk now checks that record every minute. Smaller fixes: a job
run started by hand no longer counts as the job's word; a commit dated in the future can no longer
hold off the 30-minute rule; a pull request that reached the desk's read limit keeps counting until
it changes; a job run that did nothing no longer stops the desk confirming the permission; and
tapping a notification for a pull request being recorded opens it.

As you chose, a pull request the automatic job will merge by itself, such as the one recording your
answer or filing a question, no longer counts as waiting on you while the job may still merge it. It
shows under Merges as "Being recorded by the automatic job", and the desk can read "Quiet". If the
job leaves it for you, for example because a check failed, it counts again within about a minute of
your phone being told, sometimes before. The desk also counts a little more than your phone in three
cases: a new such pull request, for a minute or two until the desk has checked it; every such pull
request for that minute or two each time you open the desk; and one the job will try again, at once.
And once the job has left one for you, the desk keeps counting it, with "The automatic job left this
for you", until its contents change or it merges, even when the job's next try would merge it; that
is usually up to about 15 minutes, and only for one your phone has already told you about. The cost,
a rough estimate: for each such pull request, and for each device with the desk open, about 5 to 20
GitHub reads that count against your hourly limit and about 1 to 3 more desk calls; there are
usually a few such pull requests a day. That is up to about two and a half times the question's
"about 5 to 8 more GitHub reads per pull request", and the question did not mention the desk calls.
On top of that, while one is open, the desk asks GitHub about four quick "has anything changed?"
questions once a minute, inside the check it already makes; GitHub's documentation says an unchanged
answer is free, and even if it were not, it would use about 240 of your 5,000 an hour. Nothing here
is irreversible, and what notifies does not change.

**The waiting-on-you screen as a board (amendment of 2026-10-19; draft 3).**

*From 2026-10-20 its build is no longer on hold and both of its open questions are answered: "The desk as
mockup v2, in stages", below, carries it on, and where the two differ that amendment governs. This
amendment is kept as it was written.*

First, what failed. Draft 2 passed the Critic's check, but the plan review failed it on one point,
now fixed: a read that kept failing could have been retried every minute without end, which on a bad
day could have pushed the desk past its daily limit of calls; it now stops after at most 5 tries for
each change, however often you mark the card, and the worst day stays under the limit. Both checks
of draft 1 failed. The worst finding: after you asked for changes on a pull request, the board would
still have offered you its merge, the same mistake as on 19 October in a new form; and for some code
changes it would have said "no verdict needed" when one was. Both are fixed: a merge is offered only
after your verdict reads PASS, and when GitHub's own check can't say, the card opens the pull
request and says what to do. For most changes to the desk's own code that will be the usual card
today, "Open", with "GitHub flagged a change to this project's code or checks: look at the changes,
then merge or add your verdict", because GitHub's check stands aside whenever that code changes; a
later governance change could narrow that, and those cards would then show "Merge" with no change
here. Draft 1 had also dropped what a gate card's details show (the case summary, its links, the
Critic's view, what happens after each answer); they are back. The build is on hold until the design
audit you asked for gives a direction, so the board's sizes and layout may still change; how it
works will not. Two questions are still open with you: one board for all your projects or one per
project, and whether a card you've just moved to Done keeps its button until GitHub confirms it;
until you answer, the plan follows each question's default, one board and the button kept. Earlier
failures, for the record: on 19 October three of the things waiting on you were pull requests that
needed only your merge, but the desk offered a verdict on every pull request and no plain "merge it"
step, so you wrote three verdicts and none was merged; and your approval of the board's final look
was asked in the session without being filed first as a question, a slip by your Chief of Staff,
recorded word for word instead. What changes: in the trial view, the waiting-on-you screen becomes a
board, three lanes side by side, "Waiting on you", "Kicked back" and "Done". Each card has one
button for the one step that clears it: "Merge" opens the pull request; "Verdict" shows only when
the pull request's risk needs your verdict, and a "Merge" card follows once your verdict reads PASS;
a question's card opens its details, with one button per option, each opening a fully written
answer, the recommendation labelled but never chosen; a waiting deploy has "Approve". As your ruling
chose, the text box you typed your own words into goes: you can still change the text on GitHub
before you commit it. Drag a card to Done, or tap "Done ✓" in its details, and it is done at once
and leaves your counts; while it waits for GitHub, your Home screen says "Nothing waiting on you ·
confirming with GitHub" instead of "Quiet". The desk then checks GitHub for that one step as often
as it already reads it; if after about 5 minutes GitHub still doesn't show it, the card moves to
"Kicked back" with the reason and counts again. Expect two kinds to be kicked back first and then
move to Done by themselves: an answer to an operating-model question given in your session, which
takes longer than 5 minutes to reach GitHub, and a held loop, whose checks take 2 to 20 minutes to
run again. If something you marked done needs you again, it leaves Done and waits on you again. Done
keeps the last 24 hours. Your Done marks are kept on that device only, since the desk can't write
anything; your other devices catch up once GitHub confirms. Pull requests the automatic job merges
itself, and questions being asked or recorded in your session, stay out of the lanes, each as one
quiet line. Your phone's notifications don't change, and your accepted views stay as they are until
the chosen design moves into the desk. In your operating-model project, which is private, the desk
doesn't read GitHub's own verdict check, so it goes by the files changed and says so on the card.
Nothing here is irreversible: a Done mark can be undone until GitHub confirms it, and the board can
be changed again.

**The desk as mockup v2, in stages (amendment of 2026-10-20; draft 4).**

After stage 1a was built, its two reviews found six places where this spec was unclear or said
two things. They are settled, and none needed you. The one you'll see: a pull request's card
doesn't yet say "check failing", because the desk doesn't read a pull request's own checks; its
details say so and point to GitHub. The rest are the desk's bookkeeping: its limit on repeated
reads now carries over from one opening to the next, so its daily cost stays under the promise;
the gate card's Critic line says the Critic's view is on GitHub until stage 4 shows its word; a
failed read of GitHub's owner check is tried again five minutes later; and two type sizes are
put right.

Draft 3 failed both checks too, on two points, and you chose "A. Fix and confirm": I fix both and
the small notes, a fresh reviewer checks only those fixes, and then building starts
(decisions/questions/P-001-desk-v2-plan-stop.md). First, the "With the agents" line missed most of
the pull requests it was written for. The desk read GitHub's owner check only for pull requests
that don't need you by their files, yet GitHub posts "Owner: after agents" only on ones that do.
It now reads that check for those too, still at most three pull requests a project, so no call is
added. What it costs instead: with those pull requests taking the three places too, a later pull
request is left fourth more often, and a fourth isn't read, so it can show as a card it doesn't
need (marked "not read yet", or not seen to be with the agents): a needless card, never a hidden
one. One limit stays, and you should know it: for a change to a project's code or checks (most
of the Builders' pull requests here), GitHub's check says only "CI code changed · check the PR",
never "Owner: after agents". So once its reviewers have passed such a pull request, it shows as a
card and your phone notifies while the agents are still fixing it, as today: a needless card,
never a hidden one. Second, I had written that your phone's new GitHub reads hold nothing up. Not
quite. The phone's sender shares an hourly GitHub allowance, and when that runs low it pauses
sending, so in a busy hour (one on 19 Oct had 58 runs) the new reads could bring that pause
sooner. The sender now makes these reads last in each run and skips them when its allowance runs
low. In a busy hour it can still pause sending, for up to about an hour: nothing is lost, it sends
on a later run, and the board isn't affected. Smaller fixes: Home from stage 2 has no "Work ahead
›" link, since the Plan tab replaces it; the phase line's words are defined exactly; the other
project screens and the links into the board are settled for the first stages; and the plan's
bookkeeping is brought up to date.

Draft 2 also failed both checks, and nothing was built from it. Three things mattered. First, it
didn't say what a project's own screens do in the first two stages, before stage 3 brings the new
project page: from the first stage those screens lose their own bar at the bottom, so only the new
bar Home · Waiting · Plan shows there, and they keep Status, Timeline and Team, with a "Waiting"
link that opens the board showing only that project, in a row at their top; stage 3 replaces them.
Second, it listed the Chief of Staff's sessions under "Since you last looked" on Home, against your
ruling that they show on the Team screen only; they are no longer listed. Third, a reviewer's
verdict file with an invisible stray character (a space after "PASS", a Windows line ending, a
hidden mark at its start) would have read as neither pass nor fail, so a pull request that needs
you could have sat in "With the agents" for good; the desk now reads every verdict file with the
reader it already has, which reads them as GitHub's own check does. Smaller fixes: Home's project
groups follow the mockup (your active projects, then "Closed or not run by the desk", both open,
then Done, closed); the Team screen's phase line reads the same as the project page's; your phone's
sender looks at GitHub's owner check for the same pull requests the board does, so the two judge
alike; and the phone's GitHub reads and the desk's costs are stated more plainly (one claim about
the phone's reads was still too hopeful; draft 4 corrects it, above).

Draft 1 had failed on four things, fixed in draft 2 and kept here: I had left out two things you
asked for (the "Latest" bubble on each Home tile, and the short line saying the phase atop the
Timeline and Team), which you have now ruled on (drop the bubble; keep the line); the new "With the
agents" line could have hidden a pull request that needs you, if one GitHub read failed just after
the agents' last commit, and now the desk never carries that judgement over to a new commit; your
phone's sender would have made thousands of extra GitHub reads a day, and now remembers what it has
read; and the cost was counted too low: the desk's calls on a busy day come to about 9,817 of the
10,000 we allow ourselves, still inside, with less room. All eleven of your answers of today are
built in, so no stage waits on a question. And since you accepted "The desk's look and screens
chosen" (MD2) today ("building it is MD3"), every stage serves "The chosen design running on the
real back end" (MD3).

Two things to know before the first stages reach your preview. The first two stages, the board and
your phone's sender, go to your preview in one deploy: when the board's pull request merges, GitHub
asks you to approve a preview deploy; leave that one unapproved until the sender's pull request has
merged too, then approve the deploy that carries both. Your phone's sender runs from the main
branch, so it takes the new rule when its pull request merges, a little before you approve that
deploy; in between, the board still shows as cards a few pull requests your phone has stopped
notifying for: the board shows more, never less. And the operating-model project's phone
notifications keep the old rule until the
Chief of Staff moves that project's copy of the sender (its own reviewed step, after the sender's
pull request): until then your phone may notify you of a pull request there that the board shows
with the agents, a needless notification, never a missed one. One part can't be done yet: the desk
can't read your portfolio, because nothing connects it, so this plan says how it will be read and
what you set up for it (adding the portfolio to the desk's read access on GitHub); until then the
portfolio's part of Home says so in plain words, and its other parts show what the desk can
already read.

What changes: as you ruled, mockup v2 is the plan for the whole desk. It is built in your trial
view in eight stages, each tried on the preview before the next. First the board, which becomes the
Waiting tab: one board for all your projects, each project's cards together under its name, a tap on
a name showing only that project, with the bar Home · Waiting · Plan at the bottom. Then Home: a
short briefing of what needs you, what changed since you last looked, with "Mark as seen", and one
full-width tile per project with its summary and its phases drawn as a timeline, left to right, with
no "Latest" bubble. Then each project's page: one
sentence, the phase strip, your milestones and the model's standard ones together on one line per
phase, and the Timeline in mockup v2's cleaner style, with Technical, Context and Why as grey words
and one short line saying the phase at its top, as on the Team screen.
Then the question and gate details; then Plan, which is your Work ahead in its own tab; then the
portfolio's read-only part at Home's foot; then every screen in dark mode; and last, the move of the
finished design into the desk itself. Your later rulings change the board as it was planned in four ways:
a pull request waiting on a reviewer's verdict, or one GitHub's owner check marks as waiting on the
agents' fixes, is no longer a card but sits in the quiet line "With the agents", and your phone
stops notifying for it until it needs you (in the operating-model project once its sender is moved,
above; GitHub's check can't mark a change to a project's code or checks so, and the desk can't read
it for the private operating-model project, so there only a missing or failing reviewer's verdict
moves a pull request into that line, the limit above); a gate card shows its four
choices as buttons on the card itself; a card you move to Done keeps its button until GitHub
confirms it; and the board is one for
all projects, grouped by project. The text box for your own words comes back in a question's and a
gate's details, as mockup v2 draws it, while each answer button still opens a fully filled-in answer.
The desk uses IBM Plex, served by the desk itself, so no font comes from another site. The points
the mockup or the rulebook left open were put to you as eleven questions, and you chose the
recommended answer to each; each is built as you answered. Nothing here is irreversible: it changes
the trial view, your accepted views stay as they are until the last stage, and each choice can be
changed again.

One planned step was dropped, as you ruled: the 5-second glance test is not run. Its plan is kept
and marked withdrawn, never run. Nothing else failed. You accepted MD3 on 23 Oct, so this revision
writes down what you ruled while the new desk was built, and plans the work that follows. On each
team member's running log, the lanes are told apart by three greys and three line styles. The desk
as built is your
desk, and a saved record of the old screens stands in for drawing them. The work ahead comes in
eight small steps. Each is one pull request you can try on the preview:
- a project the desk can't read always says since when;
- a half-written answer and your place on the screen survive the phone reloading the desk;
- each "not yet" reason is said once per group;
- the Team screen folds idle members into one line;
- the copy route sits inside each choice;
- the audit's small wording and drawing points;
- the portfolio's reads;
- last, tests and tools, with nothing on screen changed.

None of it is irreversible. Three points need you, and the Chief of Staff will put them to you.
First, whether an agent can be trusted not to hide a pull request from you through GitHub's owner
check. Second, whether more of the desk's code that your phone's sender runs should need your
approval. Third, whether this work gets a milestone of its own. Your open choice on where the
portfolio's marks sit stays open. Until you answer it, they stay as built.

## Value targets this spec traces to
V1 to V5 are the brief's (docs/PROJECT.md §6, lines 177–181 at 3117150). V5 was added by the owner and is
confirmed in this form:

V5: Owner response time: the median time from a card appearing in a connected project to its answer being committed, counting only 07:00 to 22:00 Monday to Friday (America/Chicago), with a card still open at the window's end counted at its wait so far, tracked and shown on the desk, under 4 hours, over the first 14 days after launch, 2026-11-25 (14 days after V4's date; moves with it)

- **Ruling:** decisions/questions/P-001-build-path.md, question 3 (the measure, "tracked", and the
  goal of under 4 hours on weekdays).
- **Confirmed** (decisions/questions/P-001-s001-owner-questions.md, answer 1: "confirm as
  recommended"):
  - **the window and date:** the 14 days after launch, ending 2026-11-25;
  - **open cards:** an open card counts with its wait so far;
  - **the counting clock:** only 07:00–22:00, Monday to Friday, in America/Chicago. Nights and
    weekends don't count.

  These are J7's settings (`ownerTimeZone`, `v5Clock`). The footer (AC21) carries no
  "(provisional)" label.
- **Recorded in PROJECT.md §6** (Setup CS2, done): the V5 line above is docs/PROJECT.md:181 (line 170
  when CS2 was done).
- **The display time zone** is America/Chicago too (same ruling).
- **Terms for V5:**
  - **Card appearing:** the `time` of the dispatch-log `card` entry (J2).
  - **Answer:** the `time` of the dispatch-log `decision` entry for the card's answer record.
  - **Counted time:** the length of the overlap between [appearing, answer) and the `v5Clock`
    windows, in `ownerTimeZone` (J2 gives the computation).

## Terms used in this spec
- **Connected project:** an entry in `src/config/projects.json` (J7) that the read token can read.
  At launch there are two: Service-Desk (operating model v3: `status/`, `queue/`, `dispatch-log/`)
  and Personal-Org-Operating-Model (governed under v2.5.1, with `docs/sprints/` and
  `docs/LEDGER.md`, and no `status/`, `queue/` or `dispatch-log/`; checked 2026-10-06 at 677fe5a).
  The design is sized for up to 5.
- **Model of a project:** `v3` or `v2.5`, set in J7. It decides which records J9 reads.
  - v3 projects get the full pipeline view.
  - v2.5 projects get the **reduced view** (J9): sprint, headline and "next" from the ledger, with
    PRs, questions and CI. They have no per-item stages and no "running now", because v2.5.1
    records neither.
- **Card:** a file `queue/<item>-<gate>-<n>.md` directly under `queue/` in a v3 project, written by
  the Orchestrator. Its **answer** is `decisions/<item>/<gate>-<n>.md`, which is also the path the
  card names on its own `answer:` line (J2). Card files are kept after answering: on 2026-10-06 all
  12 cards in Service-Desk `queue/` have answer files.
- **Hold card** (from M2, AC46): a file `queue/ci-hold-<sha12>.md` in a v3 project, written by the
  Orchestrator when its loop has held for over 60 minutes because the latest governance run on the
  default branch's tip is not green (governance/checks/orchestrator_git.py:1198 and :1233–1245). It
  has no answer file: the owner fixes or re-runs the governance run. J2 says when it is open.
- **Merge card** (from M2, AC47): a file `queue/<item>-merge-conflict.md` or
  `queue/<item>-merge-by-hand.md` in a v3 project, written by the Orchestrator's merge gate when a
  finished item can't be merged without the owner (orchestrator_git.py:2737 and :2887–2910). It has
  no answer file: the owner merges the item by hand or changes it. J2 says when it is open.
- **Owner question:** a file `questions/<name>.md` (`<name>` holds no `/`) other than
  `questions/_TEMPLATE.md`, in either model, in the form of `questions/_TEMPLATE.md`
  (`# Ruling needed:`, `WHY:`, `OPTIONS:`, `RECOMMENDATION:`, `RISK CLASS:`, `DEFAULT:` and
  `TIMEOUT:`; J2). In a v3 project from model v3.5.0 (S-033, L-0016, 2026-10-17) the template
  adds a `Milestone:` line and a `## Context` section (J2), and every ask of the owner, one put
  in a session included, is filed this way first.
  - **Its answer (v3 projects):** `decisions/questions/<name>.md`, whose first line is
    `Ruling: <choice>`. That is how questions are answered today:
    - Service-Desk e012edb added `decisions/questions/Q-005-sources.md`, whose line 1 is
      `Ruling: A`, and deleted `questions/Q-005-sources.md` in the same commit;
    - f45d10e did the same for `P-001-acting-route` and `P-001-planning-scope`.
  - **When it is open:** while the question file exists and no answer file exists.
  - **v2.5 projects:** there the ruling goes to the ledger, and the file is deleted
    (Personal-Org-Operating-Model f2ac482 recorded the rulings on Q-005 to Q-014 as L-0017 to L-0026
    and deleted `questions/Q-005-…` to `questions/Q-014-…`). So in v2.5 a question is open while its
    file exists.
- **Needs the owner (flagged):** exactly these four things, in a connected project, and, from
  2026-10-18, a fifth (below).
  - An open card: a card with no answer file on the default branch, or an open hold card or merge
    card (J2, from M2).
  - An open owner question (above).
  - An open, non-draft pull request whose base is the project's default branch, except one the
    Orchestrator merges itself (head branch `item/<id>` in a v3 project: the merge gate merges item
    branches, model S-013 AC3), and, from 2026-10-19, one the asks-merge job may still merge itself
    (AC79: "Being recorded by the automatic job"). The owner's own PRs count: agents push under the
    owner's account, and GitHub won't let them request the owner's review (P-001-build-path.md,
    question 1). From stage 1a of "The desk as mockup v2" in the trial view, and from stage 1b for
    the phone, a pull request with the agents (below) is not one: it is counted in "With the agents"
    until it needs the owner (AC80, J22's rule 0). The accepted views count it as before until stage
    8 makes the trial view the desk (AC43, AC44's step 4).
    - **What the repositories show (2026-10-06, REST `pulls?state=all` and `pulls/<n>`; observed,
      C):** the two repositories hold 53 PRs (33 in Service-Desk, 20 in
      Personal-Org-Operating-Model).
      - Every one was opened by the owner's account (`shumpmaster`) against `main`, with no
        requested reviewers.
      - Every one has been merged, each by `shumpmaster`. None was merged by the Orchestrator.
      - None came from an `item/` branch.
    - So in practice every such PR waits on the owner's approval or merge.
  - A v3 status file in state `waiting-owner` whose card file is not yet on the default branch. This
    is a safety net against a missed decision, worded "waiting on you: card <gate>-<n> (card file
    not found)".
  - *From 2026-10-18* (decisions/questions/P-001-notify-deploys.md, line 1, merged in pull request
    #103: "Ruling: A — a deploy waiting for the owner's approval notifies the owner and counts as
    waiting on the owner on the desk now; if another project adds deploys, it is put to the owner
    again"; the owner's answer "A. Notify and count now (Recommended)"): a workflow run whose `status` is `waiting`, in a
    project whose J7 entry has `"deploysNeedOwner": true` (Service-Desk only; AC52's Deploys).
    This changes the 16 October ruling for Service-Desk
    (decisions/questions/P-001-design-lab-answers-followup.md, answer 1).
  - *From 2026-10-20, once J23 reads the portfolio (stage 6b):* a decision card in the portfolio's
    queue (AC87). The portfolio is not a connected project, and no sender notifies it yet (AC87).
- **Activity:** anything shown but not flagged. That covers:
  - CI results.
  - Draft PRs, PRs whose base is not the default branch, and `item/` PRs in v3 projects.
  - Dispatch-log events: dispatches, outcomes, errors, retries and anomalies.
  - Sessions that run past their time limit.
  - Queue files that can't be parsed.
  - The Chief of Staff's `-notes.md` files.

  "A gate catching a problem, or an agent retrying, is activity" (PROJECT.md Part 2).
- **Open window:** a span during which the desk page is visible in the foreground on a device (the
  browser's page-visibility state is "visible").
- **An opening** (draft 8; AC77, AC78, J6, J21): the page's life on a device from its load to its
  unload, through any number of open windows. A `?open=` arrival (AC74), whether it loads the
  page or reaches a page already loaded (a service worker focusing and navigating an open desk,
  or the address handed to one), and a return to the foreground (`visibilitychange` to
  visible) start no new opening, but each runs AC77's closed read again (AC77). A `?open=` arrival
  runs it at once, in a blob call of its own; a return to the foreground polls at once only if the
  project's last poll started 60 seconds ago or more, and otherwise at that poll's 60-second
  mark, the closed read riding that poll, so A2's one poll a minute holds (draft 9, Desk 5).
- **Read successfully:** both of these hold.
  - The project's last poll call (J6) returned `state` `ok` or `unchanged`, and the page parsed
    it without error.
  - Every blob call that the poll's tree change needed has returned `ok`.

  An `unchanged` answer (every steady-poll request returned 304) counts: GitHub answered and
  nothing was new. These do not count: `partial`, `cant-read`, a 403 from the function, a Cloudflare
  error, a network failure and a page error (J6's `page` reason).
- **Quiet:** no flagged item in any connected project, **and** every connected project read
  successfully within the last 3 minutes; from 2026-10-20, once J23 reads the portfolio, also no
  card in its queue and the portfolio read successfully within the last 6 minutes (AC87).
- **Milestone accepted:** four steps, in order (P-001-build-path.md, question 0; the deploy route
  in "Toolchain and deploy route").
  1. The Reviewer's verdict on the milestone's pull request is PASS.
  2. The owner has merged it.
  3. The owner has approved desk-deploy's `preview` job for that merge, and it has deployed `main`
     to the preview.
  4. The owner has tried the preview and accepted the milestone.

  Problems found on the preview are fixed forward, in a new pull request, which also needs the
  Reviewer's PASS. MD adds its own steps before the owner accepts (AC44 steps 1–6).
- **Design lab:** MD's process A. Mockup pages the Chief of Staff publishes as private live pages,
  filled with a snapshot of real records and changed from the owner's plain-language requests and
  screenshots. No pull request or deploy; not desk code.
- **Sandbox view:** MD's process B. A view inside the desk, entered by `?sandbox`, that renders the
  chosen candidate designs against the desk's live data on the preview. It is built, reviewed and
  deployed like any other desk code.
- **Decision kind:** what sort of thing waits on the owner, read from the records: a card, an owner
  question (reversible, with a default; or irreversible, never defaulting, J2), or a pull request.
- **Unknown, stale and estimated values:** "not recorded", "not available", "not given", a value
  from a read older than 3 minutes, and a figure the desk derives rather than reads (for example a
  median over open cards' waits so far).
- **Phase and phase run** (from MD, AC50; model v3.3.0, S-023, L-0008): the model's phases are
  Discovery, Design, Build, Launch, Operate and Review. The desk shows the first four, then
  **Done**, which is not a phase: where a project stands once the owner passes its Launch gate.
  A **phase run** is one pass through a phase, labelled "<Phase> i<n>" (for example "Design i2"),
  exactly as the model's timeline names it (J11).
- **Milestone** (from MD, AC50): a phase's standard milestones (the model's checklist, the same for
  every project) and the project's own (docs/PROJECT.md section 3, each led by its plain-English
  name). Milestones are level two of the breakdown, the owner's "N+2".
- **Who has the ball** (from MD, AC49; ruling 1): who is moving a project's work right now, as the
  records the desk reads show it.
- **Queue** (from MD, AC52; ruling 6): everything that needs the owner (Terms, above) in one
  project, grouped by kind of action. From 2026-10-20 the owner has ruled one board for every
  project, grouped by project ("Ruling: C — one board, grouped by project: in each lane a project's
  cards sit together under its name, and a tap on a project's name shows only that project",
  decisions/questions/P-001-board-scope.md): in the trial view a project's queue is Waiting with
  only that project shown (AC80), and from stage 1a the Queue screen is gone, its links opening
  Waiting so (AC81, "Until stage 3").
- **Response sheet** (from MD, AC52, AC53): the sheet that opens over the queue when the owner taps
  an item: its options as choices, its facts prefilled, and, where the answer is a committed file,
  a prefilled text box.
- **Board** (from 2026-10-19, AC80): the sandbox's waiting-on-you screen (one board for every
  project, grouped by project, P-001-board-scope.md, C; from 2026-10-20 the Waiting tab, AC81), shown
  as three lanes,
  "Waiting on you", "Kicked back" and "Done", with one card for each thing that needs the owner
  (above), each card offering one step. A **mark** is the owner's "done" on a card, kept on that
  device only; one GitHub doesn't confirm within `KICK_BACK_MINUTES` puts its card in "Kicked back".
  Marks never change what needs the owner, "Quiet" or what is notified.
- **With the agents** (ruled 2026-10-20; built in the trial view at stage 1a, for the phone at
  stage 1b, and in the desk's default view at stage 8; AC80, J22's rule 0): an open pull request
  waiting on a reviewer's verdict or on the agents' fixes (P-001-board-after-agents.md and
  P-001-domain-review-count.md, both A). Where it is built, it is not flagged: it shows in the quiet
  line "With the agents: <n>", and is flagged again once it needs the owner.

## Acceptance criteria (scenarios; draft — the owner approves them by merging each milestone)
Each criterion is a plain scenario. "Within 5 minutes" is V1's figure. A "phone" screen is 360 CSS
pixels wide and a "desktop" one is 1280. The tests named in J1–J10 use the real samples quoted in J2
and J9.

### M1 — Read-only status page, behind Access, on the preview (as early as possible)
*Covers D2 and D2.2, D3.1, D3.2 (reading only), D3.3, D5 and D6.1 (preview). EXP-001, EXP-002 and
EXP-004 run on the preview after M1's merge.*

*Accepted 2026-10-07 (decisions/questions/P-001-m1-accept.md): PR #40 and fix-forward PR #41,
Reviewer PASS on each (reviews/40/reviewer.md, reviews/41/reviewer.md), deployed to the preview by
the owner's approval, CS9 checked by the owner. The experiment outcomes are under "Experiments in
Build". AC1–AC15 below are unchanged except where M2 amends what they read (AC29 replaces check runs
with workflow runs).*

**What waits on the owner**
- AC1 [trace: V1 → AC1] — When a card is committed to a connected project's default branch while
  the desk is open on the owner's phone, then within 5 minutes the project's box shows it as
  waiting on the owner and the box moves to the top of the Universe screen.
- AC2 [trace: V1 → AC2] — When an open, non-draft pull request into a connected project's default
  branch exists, whoever opened it (the owner's own included), then within 5 minutes of it opening,
  or of a draft being marked ready, the desk flags it with its title and a link to it on GitHub.
  Within 5 minutes of it being merged, closed or turned back into a draft, it is no longer flagged.
  A draft PR, or a PR into any other branch, is shown as activity only. *From 2026-10-19 (AC79):*
  one the asks-merge job may still merge itself is shown, not flagged, as "Being recorded by the
  automatic job", and is flagged within about a minute of the job leaving it.
- AC3 [trace: V1 → AC3] — When an owner question file (`questions/<name>.md`, not `_TEMPLATE.md`)
  is on a connected project's default branch, then within 5 minutes the desk flags it with its
  title (the text after `# Ruling needed: `). It is no longer flagged within 5 minutes of either
  of two things: its answer file `decisions/questions/<name>.md` being committed (v3), or the
  question file being deleted (either model).
  - *From 2026-10-17 (model v3.5.0, S-033; the model 3.5.0 records revision):* in a v3 project
    every ask of the owner, one put in a session included, is filed this way first (AGENTS.md's
    S-033 paragraph; L-0016), so this is how a session's ask reaches the desk. A question in
    S-033's form (J2) is flagged by the same rule, and its `Milestone:` line and `## Context`
    section are read for the Queue (AC66). An answered question whose file is still on the
    default branch, waiting to be tidied away (S-033 AC4 kind (d)), is answered, not flagged
    (J2's rule, unchanged). A question file is on the default branch only once its pull request
    is merged; until then the open pull request is what shows (AC2).
- AC4 [trace: V1 → AC4] — When the owner opens the desk after it was closed, then the screen says
  "Checking…" and never "Quiet" until every connected project has been read successfully since
  opening. Once they all have, every flagged item in every connected project is shown.
- AC5 [trace: V1 → AC5] — When a connected project can't be read, then its box says "Can't read
  since HH:MM" with the reason in words, sorts above every box except those with flagged items, and
  the screen as a whole does not say "Quiet". The causes are:
  - token rejected or expired;
  - GitHub rate limit;
  - GitHub, Cloudflare or network error;
  - configured default branch not found;
  - more open PRs, CI runs or tree entries than one read can page through (`partial`, J1);
  - the page hit an error reading the project's records (`page`, J6);
  - no successful read for 3 minutes.
- AC6 [trace: V2 → AC6] — When a connected project has any of the following, then the desk shows it
  as activity in that project's box and does **not** flag it, count it as waiting, or move the box
  up for it. A failing default branch still orders the box by AC8's third rank; that is not a flag.
  - a failing CI result on its default-branch head (J1's reduction rule);
  - a draft PR;
  - a new dispatch-log event, including an agent's retry and an Orchestrator anomaly (J9);
  - a session running past its time limit;
  - a queue file that can't be parsed.
- AC7 [trace: V2 → AC7] — When a card's answer file is committed by any route, then within 5
  minutes the desk stops flagging that card while open, and on next opening it is not flagged.

**Seeing each project**
- AC8 [trace: V4 → AC8] — When the owner looks at the Universe screen, then each connected project
  has one box, ordered worst first: flagged, then can't-read, then default branch failing, then the
  rest by name. Each box shows:
  - its state: the flagged count, or "Can't read", or quiet;
  - its headline (J9);
  - its sprint (v2.5), or for v3 its open items with their stage names;
  - its default-branch CI result (J1).

  *From MD (AC54, 2026-10-14):* on Home the boxes sit in three groups, Active, Done, then Closed
  or not applicable, and this order holds within each group (AC35).
- AC9 [trace: V4 → AC9] — When the owner opens a v3 project's pipeline view, then it lists every
  item that has a status file (J9). For each item it shows:
  - its id and kind;
  - **its stage**, by name: 2 Shape, 3 Define, 4 Lock the checks, 5 Produce, 6 Launch, 8 Evidence;
  - **what is running now**: for `dispatched`, the role and how long it has run;
  - **what waits on the owner**: for `waiting-owner`, the card, flagged and linked;
  - **what is next**: for `ready`, the role the Orchestrator dispatches next; for `returned`, "the
    Orchestrator routes the <role>'s return (verdict <v>)";
  - "as of", the time of the item's latest dispatch-log entry.

  Finished items (`done`, `closed`) are folded into one line each, showing their outcome. A field
  the records don't give is shown as "not recorded", never guessed.
- AC10 [trace: V4 → AC10] — When the owner opens a v2.5 project, then the desk shows the reduced
  view (J9). It shows:
  - the open sprint's title;
  - the headline, the latest ledger entry's title;
  - "next", that entry's `licenses_next:` text;
  - the project's flagged PRs and questions, and its CI.

  "Items" and "running now" say "not recorded in this repository's records (operating model
  v2.5.1)".
- AC11 [trace: V1 → AC11] — When the owner taps a flagged card on the phone, then its full text is
  shown with every option it offers, rendered from its markdown, without sideways scrolling, plus
  the answer path the card names. (In M1 the desk links to the card on GitHub; answering from the
  desk is M2.)
- AC12 [trace: V1 → AC12] — When the owner taps a flagged owner question on the phone, then its
  full text is shown, rendered from its markdown, without sideways scrolling (J2). The view shows:
  - its title;
  - WHY;
  - every option under OPTIONS, with its letter and text;
  - the RECOMMENDATION, marked on its option;
  - RISK CLASS, REVERSIBILITY and BLAST RADIUS;
  - the DEFAULT, labelled "per the question file: defaults to <letter> at <raised time + TIMEOUT
    hours>" when the question is reversible, and "per the question file: never defaults" when it
    is irreversible (AGENTS.md §5).
    - The label only reports what the file says. Service-Desk does not enforce question timeouts:
      no script adopts a default. The desk must not imply that one will.

  A field the file lacks is shown as "not given". The question is still flagged.
  - **Changed by AC85 (desk mockup v2, 2026-10-20):** in the trial view a reversible question's
    default reads "Settles itself as <letter> on <when> if left (per the question file: <TIMEOUT>
    hours)", on its card "Settles as <letter> · <when>" and in Home's briefing "one question settles
    itself <when>" (frames 3b, 1 and H1), and an irreversible one "Can't be undone … Never settles
    itself: it waits for you (per the question file)" (frame 3). The sheet keeps "per the question
    file" and says how a question settles (AC85), so the rule above, that the desk implies nothing
    more, stands.

**Trust, budget and the first deploy**
- AC13 [trace: V4 → AC13] — When any request reaches the desk's function without a valid
  `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` for the owner's email address, then it answers 403 and makes no GitHub
  call. "Not valid" covers a JWT that is missing, expired, for the wrong audience, wrongly signed, or
  for another email. A `POST` without `Content-Type: application/json`, or with a foreign `Origin`,
  is refused (J6's request checks). The preview's `pages.dev` address and its preview deployments
  prompt for Access login before anything is served. The Reviewer's security review of the login and of the
  read token's handling (D5.2) has passed before M1 is accepted.
- AC14 [trace: V4 → AC14] — *Limit: the hosting spend ceiling of $0 a month (PROJECT.md §5,
  decisions/questions/P-001-move-to-build-values.md). The trace checker accepts only V targets, so
  the formal trace is to V4, the replacement within its limits.* When the desk's open windows add
  up to 16 hours in a day across all devices, with 5 connected projects, then the function stays
  within the Free plan:
  - fewer than 10,000 function requests that day (our own margin, a tenth of Free's 100,000);
  - no Error 1027;
  - no Error 1102 on any call.

  The same holds on such a day when every J12 read fails all day for all 5 projects (from
  2026-10-17, the desk follow-ups; build review round 2 of trial-view notes 2, N1). A failed J12
  read is retried with J12's backoff, never on every cycle, so the day makes at most 5,715 calls.
  The arithmetic and its assumptions are in "Facts relied on". A day with more than 16 window-hours
  is outside this scenario: only staying under Free's 100,000 is promised for it.
  - **Test:** a test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC14` drives the page's real poll scheduler with a fake
    clock and a fake function. It simulates 5 connected projects for 16 window-hours, with 10
    openings and 100 head changes. It asserts that fewer than 10,000 function calls are made and
    that none is a retry sooner than the next poll. From 2026-10-17 it runs the same day again
    with J12 failing:
    - all 5 projects are v3 projects in the sandbox, so each makes J12's reads;
    - the fake function fails every J12 read all day: `"pulls": null` in one run, and a
      `data: null` answer in another;
    - it asserts fewer than 10,000 calls, and no J12 read sooner than J12's backoff allows;
    - it asserts at most 43 J12 reads a project after a failed one. Each opening's first J12 read
      is not counted, so a project makes at most 53 J12 reads in all (plan review round 1 of the
      desk follow-ups, N6).

    From 2026-10-19 (AC79; draft 4) it runs the notifications case again with each of the 288 pull
    request heads a job candidate, in all 5 projects, with J12 failing in all 5, one log read and
    the grant read failing all day, 100 ledger changes, and 5 candidate heads per project open
    across all 10 openings: it asserts fewer than 10,000 calls (A3's sum, 7,577); no AC79 blob call
    in a poll whose conditional reads all answered 304; at most 3 AC79 blob calls per candidate head
    in an opening, the failing one included; the failed grant read asked again only at the next
    opening or ledger change; and each completed run's log read at most once per opening. From
    2026-10-19 (AC80) the same days run again with 3 open pull requests a project on the board, each
    with an owner-check read and one mark kicked back and marked again, and then the worst case of
    A3's board additions: a mark on each of the 288 pull request heads with its J20 read failing all
    day, and a verdict commit on each: it asserts fewer than 10,000 calls (A3's 9,355); at most 5
    waited-read calls per pull request head over the whole day, across all 10 openings (the count
    kept on the device, AC80), a re-mark from "Kicked back" on each head included,
    none after that bound and none for a kicked-back card; at most one first verdict-blob call per
    verdict commit and per opening per project, its retries inside the head's 5; and J1's 30
    requests per poll call held. From 2026-10-20 (desk mockup v2) that worst case runs again with
    the portfolio connected and read every 5 minutes for the 16 hours, every head change carrying
    J24's commits read and its reviewers' verdict files, and 5 open pull requests a project, each
    with verdict files on its branch and updated since "last looked", at each of the 10 openings: it
    asserts fewer than 10,000 calls (A3's 9,817); at most one verdict call per pull request head in
    an opening besides the one in its verdict commit's cycle, its retries inside the head's 5, and a
    failing verdict blob failing only its own head's call; J24's pages riding the head's J20 call at
    a head change, with no call of their own, and adding at most one call a project an opening; and
    the portfolio's poll at most once in 5 minutes after each opening's first read, with at most one
    cold portfolio blob call an opening (each bound as A3 counts it, plan review note 3, round 1);
    and, from draft 3 (the plan review's notes 2 and 7, round 2), at most 16 blob calls in any one
    cycle for a project (A3: 6 + 2 × 5), and J24's commits read failing at every opening with its
    retries adding no call.

    **Each of these is one combined day** (stage 1a's build review, round 1, finding 3, which found
    the board's cases run on a day without AC79's): the board's additions, and mockup v2's on top
    of them, run in the same simulated day as AC79's case itself, with its 288 candidate heads, J12
    failing in all 5 projects and the log read and the grant read failing all day, never on a day
    without them, so "fewer than 10,000" bounds A3's 9,355 and 9,817 as A3 counts them. In that
    day the waited J20 reads fail at every opening, so a head open across openings is waited on in
    each, and the test asserts at most 5 waited-read calls a head for the day; and the same day
    runs once more with local storage throwing, asserting no waited-read call at all and fewer
    than 10,000 calls.

### M2 — Answering cards, time asked, agent usage and context windows; CI and robustness
*Covers D3.2 and D4.1 (answering), D3.5, V5 and D3.6, plus what M1's acceptance carried forward:
CI from workflow runs (AC29) and the Reviewer's PR #41 findings (AC30–AC34); and the
Orchestrator's hold cards and merge cards (AC46, AC47), so nothing that waits on the owner shows
only as "can't parse". EXP-003 runs at M2's
start. M2 also records the EXP-002 and EXP-004 results in `docs/handover/experiments/` (Brief).*

- AC16 [trace: V4 → AC16] — When the owner picks an option on an open card (and optionally types a
  note), then the desk opens GitHub's new-file page for that card's repository and default branch.
  The page has the file name `decisions/<item>/<gate>-<n>.md` and J3's content filled in, and the
  owner commits it there; the desk itself writes nothing to GitHub. If the answer file already
  exists, the desk shows "already answered: <verdict>" and offers no link.
- AC17 [trace: V4 → AC17] — When the prefilled link would be longer than the cap
  (`linkCap` in J7, 6,000 characters; EXP-004 found every length up to 8,000 opened, so the cap
  keeps a margin), or that repository's
  `contentPrefill` is `false` (J7), then the desk instead shows the answer text with a "Copy" button
  and opens the new-file page with only the file name filled in.

  - "retry" when it re-dispatches a role whose previous session ended in `error`.

- AC23 [trace: V4 → AC23] — When a session's record carries usage figures (J10, in model S-020's
  form), then the Agents view shows, for that session, behind the session's drill-down (tapping the
  session), not on its timeline row, so the timeline stays readable on the phone:
  - its tokens by kind (input, output, cache read, cache write: J10's `input_tokens`,
    `output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`);
  - its turns (`num_turns`);
  - its run time as the agent tool reports it (`duration_ms`, rounded to the nearest second);
  - its peak context-window use as tokens and as a percentage of the window (`context_peak`,
    `context_window`), labelled "derived from per-turn usage" when J10's `derived` names it;
  - the peak also as a percentage of the compaction threshold (`context_peak` over
    `autocompact_threshold`; the owner's answer 5 is about stopping before compaction);
  - "would have stopped: yes" or "no" (`would_have_stopped`);
  - the compaction count (`compactions`);
  - the agent tool's cost estimate as "estimate $x.xx" (`cost_usd_estimate`, two decimals), never
    presented as a charge: the account is billed by subscription.

  **One rule for missing figures, everywhere in the desk:**
  - **"not recorded":** the outcome line has no `usage` key. That is a session that ran before
    model S-020 was adopted (L-0005), an Orchestrator `error` line (no session ran, S-020 AC2), or a
    line whose `usage` `record` dropped as malformed (S-020 AC2, "NOTE: usage dropped"). A single
    `usage` key with a value of the wrong kind (J10) is also "not recorded", for that figure only;
    the rest of the line still shows.
  - **"not available":** the figure is `null` in `usage`, a field the agent tool doesn't report
    (EXP-003), per the owner's O6 fallback (decisions/questions/P-001-o6-fallback.md, option A).
    A percentage is "not available" unless both its figures are present (not null), and also
    when its divisor (`context_window` or `autocompact_threshold`) is 0, since it can't be
    computed; the figures themselves still show. This covers
    the threshold percentage, "would have stopped" and the compaction count too: at the pinned
    agent-tool version all three are null on today's real lines.
  - **One exception, the Chief of Staff's session lines** (from 2026-10-17, J13): a `null`
    figure there, in an end line's `usage` or a helper line's `reported`, reads "not recorded",
    not "not available", as model S-033's J3 pins it: no tool gives a conversational session
    its own figures, so it is a figure no record holds, not one an agent tool left out.

  No paid route is used to get a missing figure.

**Carried from M1's acceptance** (P-001-m1-accept.md, "Carried to M2")
- AC29 [trace: V4 → AC29] — When the owner looks at a connected project's CI result (AC8's box,

    Personal-Org-Operating-Model the check-runs read answers 403, so its CI line reads "can't read
    checks" on the preview today (P-001-m1-accept.md).
  - **With the read token holding Actions: read** (Setup G3, the owner's step): both projects' CI
    lines show `passing`, `failing`, `running` or `none` by J1's reduction rule.
  - **Without it** (a 403 on the workflow-runs read only): CI shows "can't read CI (the read token
    needs Actions: read)", and the project stays readable, as J1 says.
  - **Covered on every head:** push runs and `workflow_dispatch` runs are both read, so a head the
    Orchestrator made (whose governance run is a dispatch run) shows its governance result, and a

  - desk-deploy and Orchestrator runs are activity, not CI (J1).
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC29` uses recorded workflow-runs responses, including the real

- AC30 [trace: V1 → AC30] — When one connected project's records hold something the page can't

  - **A failure while drawing** its box shows that box as "Can't show this project: <error in
