**The project screens, after the owner's trial-view notes** (added 2026-10-15)
*From notes 6 to 15 of the same record (decisions/questions/P-001-trial-view-notes-1.md), read as
its "How it is read" lines read them, and the owner's answer on note 7. Notes 10 to 13 and 15
change AC49, AC51, AC52 and AC53 in place; the two criteria below carry the rest. Where AC48 and
these differ, these govern.*

- AC55 [trace: V4 → AC55] — When the owner opens a project's Status screen in the sandbox, then a
  "Your last action" line, just above the bar that says whether anything waits on the owner, names
  the owner's most recent recorded action in that project, and "More detail" opens the Pipeline,
  Time asked and Agents views drawn in the new design inside the sandbox.
  - **Changed by AC83 (desk mockup v2, 2026-10-20):** in the trial view "Your last action" sits
    under the project page's phase strip (frame 5), and "More detail"'s views open from the page's
    "Details" row (AC83); the views themselves are unchanged, on AC81's tokens from stage 7 (AC88).
  - **"Your last action"** (note 6: "Right above that bar, can you record my last action or
    decision just so I can orient to it quickly").
    - **What it names:** the latest, by its time, of the owner's recorded actions in that project
      the desk reads:
      - **a card answer:** the dispatch log's `decision` entry (J2), in J9's decision words
        ("P-001: you answered dor-4 with build"), at that entry's `time`, linked to
        `decisions/<item>/<gate>-<card>.md`;
      - **a ruling:** a record `decisions/questions/<name>.md` whose line 1 starts `Ruling:`,
        or `Decision:` for a target-user profile approval (decisions/README.md), in its first
        line's words without that word (as AC52's "Done today"), at the time of its oldest
        commit (J2's history read, as AC20), linked to the file. Every other file there (a
        `-notes.md` file, a Critic's verdict such as
        `P-001-milestones-adoption-critic-1.md`) is not the owner's and is ignored, never shown
        (plan review round 1, B1).

      A record whose second line is a `Proxy:` line is marked "(proxy)": it was made at the
      owner's request, in the owner's words.
    - **Its form:** "Your last action: <words> · <time>", the time as J9 gives times, then the
      record's code. The words wrap.
    - **A long ruling line is clipped to three lines** (the owner's follow-up ruling,

**The Status and Timeline screens, after the owner's trial-view notes 2** (added 2026-10-16)
*From the owner's notes of 2026-10-16, notes 1 to 27 of decisions/questions/P-001-trial-view-notes-2.md,
read as its "How it is read" lines read them, later readings replacing earlier ones where they say
so; and from the design the owner approved there, mockup version 6
(docs/design/mockups/status-and-timeline.html) and, for the Home tile,
docs/design/mockups/phase-branches.html. The owner's words are quoted exactly as written, typos
included. Where AC48, AC50 or AC51 and these differ, these govern. Every count, date and word
these screens show comes from a record the desk reads (J9, J10, J11, J12) or is one of the desk's
fixed labels quoted here; where a record is missing the screen says so (AC41). Nothing here is
built without `?sandbox`: the accepted M1 and M2 views stay exactly as they are (AC43).*

**Terms for these criteria:**
- **Run, on the branch drawing** (C): a column of phase runs. Take the model's timeline's phase
  runs in its order (J11). The first starts run 1. Each later phase run whose phase is the same as,
  or comes before, the phase of the run just before it starts a new run: the work went back. Every
  other phase run carries on in the run it follows. Runs are numbered from 1 in that order and
  shown as "Run <k>". For Service-Desk at 3117150 (J11's fixture): run 1 is Discovery i1, Design i1
  and Build i1; run 2 is Design i2, Build i2 and Launch i1.
- **Finished and standing:** a phase run before AC50's now run whose phase has no later run.
  At 3117150, Discovery i1.
- **Finished, then gone back over:** a phase run before the now run whose phase has a later run.
  At 3117150, Design i1 and Build i1.
- **Still to come:** a phase run after the now run. At 3117150, Build i2 and Launch i1.

- AC57 [trace: V4 → AC57] — When the owner opens a project's Status screen in the sandbox, then
  its phases read from the bottom up, Discovery at the bottom and Done at the top, each in its own
  box with its phase's colour, that folds on a tap and lists every run of that phase; one column of
  dots per run sits inside the boxes and branches right where the work went back; and every
  milestone of every run shows its state, in words, and its why line.
  - **Changed by AC83 (desk mockup v2, 2026-10-20):** in the trial view the Status screen's phase
    boxes and branch drawing give way to the project page's phase strip and its milestones by
    phase, one folded line per phase, read from the bottom up (frames 5, 6 and 6b;
    P-001-standard-milestones.md, A), and the branch drawing moves to the Home tile's timeline
    (AC82, frame H5). This criterion's rules for each run's and each milestone's state, its runs and
    its reached marks still decide what both show. Two parts go: the key above the phase boxes
    (mockup v2 draws no key; the rulebook's conflict 2, settled as drawn) and "why: not recorded" on
    every milestone, narrowed to one line per phase where no why is written yet, each milestone
    showing its why only once there is one ("Ruling: A — where no standard milestone's why is
    written yet, the phase's list says so once; each milestone shows its why only once there is
    one", P-001-why-line.md; the rulebook's spec points).
  - The owner's words:
    - note 1: "the app shows us back in a design iteration but also implies build is done?
      Chronologically that can’t be true", and its answer: "anywhere we have chronological phases
      like this, we should incorporate a branch style visual. By expanded out a second, third,
      fourth (however many are applicable) dot set to the right of the original milestone dot";
      on the mockup: "This is the exact picture I had in mind. Every box list it’s runs as well,
      but in smaller de emphasized text";
    - note 2: "when a phase was completed but branched off, make the dot fill lighter than a fully
      completed phase";
    - note 6 (the owner's point 4): "when we show the standard milestones that we DONT do for a
      particular project, it doesnt easily translate to what we DO take on - in chronologgical
      order. The other thing is that every milestone within the phases should have a short snippet
      of "why this phase was included or not included"";
    - notes 10 to 12: "maybe soften the text color for not utilized milestones and add a simple
      light directional line that ties the milestones/phases from the bottom to the top to
      indicate direction";
    - note 15: "I was always envisioning phases > milestones > tasks to read bottom up. So
      discovery would be at the bottom and the final thing done would be at the top.";
    - note 19: "reduce the weight on the line connecting things";
    - note 25: "Lets do B - simply because i like the ability to cleanly collapse and draw
      distinction between phases."
  - **Read from the bottom up** (note 15, replacing note 12's reading). From the top of the screen:
    Done, Launch, Build, Design, Discovery. Inside a box, the latest run sits at the top and the
    earlier runs below it. Inside a run, the first milestone sits at the bottom and the last at the
    top: the run's standard milestones at the bottom, in the model's order (`<Phase>-1` lowest),
    then the project's own milestones above them, in the order docs/PROJECT.md section 3 lists
    them.
  - **Each phase in its own box** (note 25, option B of note 20):
    - the box carries its phase's colour as a stripe down its left edge (note 13; AC48's phase
      colours), and its phase's name in words. Done's box is dashed with no stripe;
    - its header holds the phase's name and its state word (AC50, as changed by note 1): for
      Service-Desk at 3117150, Discovery "Finished", Design "Now · run 2", Build "Run 2 still to
      come", Launch "Not started", and Done "After the Launch gate" until the project is Done (C,
      the mockup's words);
    - the now phase's box keeps its place and is marked there, with a gold border and its state
      word (AC50's "emphasize it inline");
    - **it folds** (note 25): the phase's name is a real button, in the tab order, opened by a tap,
      a click, or Enter or Space, with the phase's name as its accessible name and its folded or
      open state as its accessible state and as a mark beside the name, never colour alone. It
      folds the box to its one header line and opens it again. Done has nothing to fold;
    - **how boxes start** (C, as the mockup draws them): open, except a phase whose every run is
      finished and standing (at 3117150, Discovery), which starts folded. Folding one box never
      moves or reorders any other, and a refresh keeps each box as the owner left it (AC56).
  - **The branch drawing** (notes 1, 2, 10, 16, 20 and 25):
    - **one column of dots per run** (Terms), run 1 furthest left and each later run one step to
      the right, at the same position across in every box. The dots sit inside the boxes, on the
      left (option B). Each dot is level with its box's phase name, centred on it (within 1 px),
      and stays so when any box folds or opens and when the width changes;
    - **which dots:** one for each phase run, in its run's column, in its phase's box. After the
      latest run's last phase run, that column carries on with a still-to-come dot in each later
      phase's box, through Done (C, as drawn: at 3117150, run 2 has dots at Design, Build, Launch
      and Done);
    - **each dot's mark, with its words in the run's line in the box (never colour alone):**
      - finished and standing: filled;
      - finished, then gone back over: a lighter fill with an outline (note 2), its run reading
        "finished, then gone back over";
      - the now run: a gold ring, when it holds the next milestone to reach (rule 2 below), so the
        ring means the same on a run as on a milestone. When AC50's now run comes from its second
        branch (every project milestone has work filed, so the now run is the one holding the
        latest recorded step), no milestone is next to reach: the now run's dot is then a
        half-filled circle, "now: work under way", and no gold ring shows (C; plan review round 2,
        N5);
      - still to come: an empty ring;
      - Done: an empty ring until the project is Done (AC50), then filled.

      With no now run (AC50's "not recorded"), every phase run's dot is a dashed ring and its words
      say "not recorded";
    - **the lines** (notes 12, 15 and 19): within a column, a thin, light line joins each dot to
      the next one up, crossing the gap between boxes, with a small arrowhead half way that points
      up. A line into a still-to-come dot is dashed. Where a run starts, one curve joins the last
      dot of the run before it to the new run's first dot, out to the right. There are no other
      slanted pieces. The lines are as thin and light as version 6 draws them after note 19: 1.25 px
      at 70% opacity (docs/design/mockups/status-and-timeline.html:581 and :587);
    - **each run's column** has its own shade (run 1 neutral, run 2 gold, as drawn), and is named
      in words on every run in the boxes ("Run 2"). The drawing itself is hidden from assistive
      technology: the words carry it. **A third or later run** (build review round 1, N4; C)
      takes a neutral-tinted shade that is none of AC48's 14 meaningful colours: run 3 a cool grey
      (light `#7b828a`, dark `#8d8d77`), run 4 a grey-olive (light `#7f8669`, dark `#c3d0c3`),
      and later runs these two in turn (run 5 as run 3, run 6 as run 4), their words telling them
      apart. Each is at least 10 by CIEDE2000 from all 14 colours and from the other in its theme
      (measured on 2026-10-16: lowest 17.7 light, 15.3 dark), and at least 3:1 in contrast against
      the page and card surfaces in its theme. AC48's test checks these four values against the 14
      and each other;
    - **a key** above the boxes, each entry with its mark (plan review round 2, B2): for the runs'
      dots, "finished · finished, then gone back over · now: holds the next milestone to reach ·
      still to come"; for the milestones, "reached · work under way · next to reach · no work
      filed yet · not reached · not taken on, or not recorded". The gold ring is named "next to
      reach" in both, never "now" alone.
  - **Every run in its box** (note 1's mockup answer 2):
    - each run opens with its tag, "Run <k>" (here and on every screen, <k> is the run in Terms
      above, the column, never the phase's iteration; plan review round 1, N4), then "<Phase> i<n> ·
      <state words>": "finished",
      "finished, then gone back over", "now", "still to come" or "not recorded" (for example
      "Run 1 · Build i1 · finished, then gone back over");
    - the latest run reads at full size; every earlier run is smaller and quieter: its text one
      role down on AC62's type scale and in the muted colour, never a size of its own.
  - **Every milestone of every run, in order** (note 6): the project milestones the model's
    timeline places in that run (J11), and every standard milestone of that phase, with its state
    for that run.
    - **Standard milestones:** a line "Standard milestones · <count by state>" ("4 reached · 4 not
      recorded"), then each one by name, its code after, and its state word: the model's (reached,
      not reached, not recorded, carried over or not needed), or "Skipped" where AC61's plan line
      says so. In the latest run of a phase every one is listed. In an earlier run those whose
      state is "not recorded" are gathered behind one line, "<n> not recorded, one tap away",

    only on the screens not yet built to mockup v2, and each stage's pull request takes its screens
    off it.
  - The owner's words: note 3, "the general spacing of things. I dont hate it, but there are spots
    that seem too spaced, and then some spots that seem too tight."; note 5, "There is a lot of
    text throughout the service desk - which i want specifically - however if all of the text is
    formatted almost identically it all kind of blurs together."
  - **One spacing scale** (note 3): 4, 8, 12, 20 and 32 px, as five tokens in `sandbox.css`, the
    mockup's `--s1` to `--s5` (docs/design/mockups/status-and-timeline.html:17). Every margin,
    padding and gap that sets the space between or around elements on every sandbox screen is 0 or
    one of the five, used so that related things sit close and separate groups sit further apart:
    4 and 8 inside an item, 12 between items of a group, 20 between groups, 32 between a screen's
    sections (C, as the mockup uses them). The only other values (C), each with a comment beside it
    in `sandbox.css` naming why, are: the page's 16 px side gutter with the safe areas (as the
    mockup draws it); the room kept for the bottom bar (`--sb-dock-h`) and the safe areas; the
    offsets that put a dot, icon or circle on its line; the 44 px touch targets (AC56), and the
    board's 36 px tap boxes, 27 px pills and its cards' and rows' tight padding of 1, 2, 5 and 6 px,
    as version 5 draws and comments them (AC80, pending the design audit of 2026-10-19); borders;
    a label chip's or tag's inner padding (as drawn, 1 px by 6 px: the mockup's `.bul .k` and
    `.bkey span`, :201 and :229); and the gap of 2 to 6 px between a mark or icon and its word
    inside one label, key entry or bullet (the mockup's `.key span` and `.bul li`, :56 and :200)
    (plan review round 1, N3). Every other spacing value in the mockups gives way to the scale.
  - **One type scale with distinct roles** (note 5): seven roles, each with its own look, their
    values the mockup's `--t-*` tokens (docs/design/mockups/status-and-timeline.html:19-25):
    - **screen title:** each screen's heading;
    - **section label:** small, upper case and spaced: group and fold headers, band names, run
      tags, the labels "Done when", "Why", "Technical" and "Context";
    - **item name:** the names of projects, phases, milestones and members, and sprint titles;
    - **body:** sentences;
    - **meta:** state words, times, dates, counts, sources and keys;
    - **quoted record text:** words quoted from a record: rulings, summaries, why lines, the
      Purpose quotes, a sprint's Why;
    - **codes:** ids such as `MD2` and `PR #61`, in monospace (AC48).

    Every font set in `sandbox.css` uses one of the seven. A role may change its colour, and an
    earlier run or a softened milestone may take the next role down (AC57), but nothing takes a size
    of its own: the mockup's own sizes (such as the sprint title's 1.04rem, :198, or the phase
    name's 1.12rem, :72) give way to the roles. The exceptions: AC63's text boxes, at least 16 px;
    the board's own sizes (AC80), version 5's `--b-*` tokens, pending the design audit of
    2026-10-19; and marks drawn as text, which are icons, not text roles (the ◆, ✓, ✕ and – glyphs,
    and `.sb-badge`'s count, sized to their icon, N3).
  - **Every word kept** (note 5: "which i want specifically"): on every sandbox screen other than
    the parts AC57 to AC60 and AC65 to AC68 rebuild or add to (the Status screen's phase list,
    Home's phase checklist, the Timeline, the Queue's rows and group icons, the Team screen's
    cards, the phase marker, "More detail"'s Pipeline link, the lines AC69 to AC72 add or
    reword, and, from draft 8 (build review round 1 of model 3.5.0's records, (b)), a v3
    project's Chief of Staff page's status line, Responsible-for groups and running log (AC49,
    J13), and, from Work ahead's draft 6 (build review round 1, note J), Home's "Work ahead ›"
    control (AC24), and, from 2026-10-19, the Queue's board (AC80)), the text is the same, word for
    word, before and after. Only the look changes.
  - Judged on the phone by the owner too: the sandbox pull request shows each screen at 360 px in
    the light and dark themes.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC62` reads `sandbox.css`, as AC51's and AC54's tests do, and
    checks that every margin, padding, gap, row-gap and column-gap is 0, one of the five tokens,
    or a value with its comment; that every `font` and `font-size` uses a role's token, the text
    box rule excepted; and that the seven tokens differ from each other. It renders every sandbox
    screen from the fixtures, and checks each screen's text, outside the rebuilt parts, against a
    snapshot taken from the same fixtures at commit 2c1acb6 (committed under
    `tests/desk/fixtures/`).

- AC70 [trace: V4 → AC70] — When the owner looks at a place where a project went back and a new
  run began, on the Status screen's branch drawing or at the Timeline's band where that run starts,
  then the reason the run began is shown there, quoted from its record, with its source and one tap
  to the whole record; or "why it went back: not recorded" where no record gives it.
  - The owner's pick: "Why it went back (Recommended)", whose option text says: "At each branch
    point on Status and the Timeline, show the ruling that sent the project back (e.g. why Design
    ran a second time). Today the drawing shows that it branched, not why."
  - **Where the model records why a run began** (model S-023 AC6; found in
    governance/checks/orchestrator.py and v3_checks.py): an item's phase run starts again only
    after a *boundary* line in the dispatch log, an applied decision whose gate word sends the work
    back through a gate it did not pass (`BOUNDARY_WORDS`: `recycle` or `re-aim` at the `dor` gate,
    `recycle` or `revise` at `criteria` and `launch`; governance/checks/orchestrator.py:130 and :284-286). That line
    names its answer record (`record`, for example `decisions/<item>/<gate>-<n>.md`), whose
    `Reason:` line is the owner's reason (decisions/README.md: hold and recycle need one). A run
    the model's timeline builds from the plan's milestone order alone, with no line of its own
    (v3_checks.py, `place_milestones`), has no such record.
  - **The rule:** for each run that starts a new column (AC57's Terms, runs 2 and later), the
    reason is the latest boundary line of the run's item before the run's first routed line. The
    desk shows:
    - "Run <k> began · <date>" (the boundary line's `time`, in `ownerTimeZone`), in its run's own
      shade (AC57's run shades; build review round 1, N4);
    - the text of its record's first `Reason:` line, quoted as written; and when the record has no
      `Reason:` line, plain words instead, with the gate's code and word after in the code role
      (AC64; plan review round 3, N4): "sent back at a gate, with no reason written" then
      `<gate>: <word>` (for example `dor: recycle`) (C);
    - its source, "your ruling · <record path>" when the line is not marked `proxy`, otherwise
      "ruling by proxy · <record path>";
    - **one tap to the whole record:** the source is a link to the record on GitHub, by AC51's
      link rule.

    With no boundary line, or a record the tree does not hold: "Run <k> began · why it went back:
    not recorded" (slate, AC69).
  - **For Service-Desk, plainly:** at 3117150 and on today's default branch, run 2 (Design i2) is
    one the model's timeline builds from the plan's order (MD1 to MD3 follow M1 to M2B in
    section 3); no boundary line starts it (tests/desk/fixtures/j11-3117150/trace-notes.txt: Build
    i1 and Design i2 hold no decision line). So the desk shows "why it went back: not recorded"
    there. The mockup's quote of decisions/questions/P-001-design-step.md is an illustration: no
    record the desk reads ties that ruling to the run. A record that did (a model change, for
    example a run's start line naming its ruling) is listed in "What this spec does not cover".
  - **Where it shows:** on Status, in the box of the phase where the new run starts, at the top of
    that run, beside the curve; on the Timeline, at the top of that run's band, under its name. The
    words are the same on both.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC70` checks "why it went back: not recorded" for Design i2 with

- AC71 [trace: V1 → AC71] — When nothing has moved on an active project for 3 days or more and
  nothing in it waits on the owner, then its Home card says so in a slate line, "No movement for
  <n> days · last: <what>, <date>".
  - The owner's pick: "Stalled-project signal", whose option text says: "If nothing has moved on a
    project for a set number of days and nothing waits on you, its tile says so ("No movement for
    5 days"), so a quiet desk can't hide a stopped project." The number: "3 days (Recommended)"
    ("Long enough to skip a quiet weekend, short enough to catch a stop within the week.").
  - **What counts as moving**, each from a record the desk reads, the latest of these being the
    project's last movement:
    - the default branch's head commit, at its `committedAt` (J6's poll answer; every merge,
      filed question, filed card and committed agent record lands as a commit there);
    - a pull request merged into the default branch, at its `mergedAt` (J12);
    - an open pull request's `updated_at` (J1's open list), for work on a branch not yet merged
      (C);
    - a dispatch-log entry, at its `time` (J9): an agent's dispatch or outcome, a card raised, a
      decision.
  - **When it shows:** the project is in the Active group (AC54), was read successfully within the
    last 3 minutes (Quiet's rule), nothing in it waits on the owner (its pill's count is 0), and
    its last movement is at least 3 days (72 hours) before now. <n> is the whole number of days
    since the last movement.
  - **"last: <what>, <date>"**, the date in `ownerTimeZone`, the words for the latest movement:
    "PR #<n> merged" (J12), "PR #<n> updated" (J1), J9's headline words for a dispatch-log entry,
    or "a commit on <default branch>" for a head commit none of the others accounts for. When two
    have the same time, the first in this list is named (C).
  - **In slate, not coral** (AC69: it is a heads-up, not a decision for the owner). It sits on the
    card under who has the ball. It changes nothing else: the card's order, its group and "Quiet"
    stay as AC8, AC54 and AC1 to AC7 have them.
  - **Not shown** for a project in Done or Closed (C), for one that can't be read, while its reads
    are not all in ("not available yet" shows nowhere for it: the line simply waits), or when
    something waits on the owner. The mockup's "Moving: last change today." line for a moving
    project is not built: the owner picked only the stalled signal (C, a known difference).
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC71` drives a fake clock over fixtures: no line at 71 hours; the
    line at 72 hours with "3 days"; each kind of movement as the latest, with its words and date;
    the tie order; no line when something waits, for a Done project, or for one that can't be
    read; the line in `--muted`; and the card's order unchanged.

- AC72 [trace: V4 → AC72] — *Traced to V4 because the desk takes over the live address only through
  deploys the owner approves; none of V1 to V5 measures a deploy's safety itself (plan review round
  3, N4).* When a deploy waits for the owner's approval in a project's Queue, then
  its row says whether the commit it would deploy is the merge commit of a pull request the
  Reviewer passed, with the source, or that it is not and should not be approved, or that the desk
  can't check yet; the approval itself stays on GitHub.
  - **Changed by AC80 (the board, 2026-10-19):** on the board, a waiting deploy is an "Approve ↗"
    card, and this criterion's row words show in its sheet, word for word (AC80). Its test runs them
    there (tests/desk/ac69-72-audit-additions.test.mjs).
  - The owner's pick: "Safe-to-approve on deploys", whose option text says: "Each deploy waiting
    for your approval shows whether it matches a pull request the Reviewer passed ("matches PR #77
    · Reviewer PASS"), so a wrong tap can't ship unreviewed code."
  - **Which commit** (plan review round 3, B1): a waiting deploy in AC52's Deploys group is a
    workflow run in J1's lists for the current head (AC52's known gap still holds: a deploy waiting
    on an earlier head drops out). The commit it would deploy is:
    - for a run started by a push (`event` `push`): its `head_sha`;
    - for a run started by hand (`event` `workflow_dispatch`, as every production deploy and every
      manual preview redeploy is): the commit the owner gave it, not `head_sha`, which is only
      main's head when it was started. J1's run list does not hold the run's inputs, but it holds
      its `display_title`, which desk-deploy sets to `deploy <sha> — <note>` for a hand-started
      run (.github/workflows/desk-deploy.yml:15, `run-name: deploy ${{ github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.sha || inputs.sha }} — …`, and from Setup CS14 `deploy <sha>` alone for a push run;
      .github/scripts/desk_pick_commit.sh:18 deploys
      `INPUT_SHA`; `display_title` is in GitHub's run list, as the recorded
      tests/desk/fixtures/github/runs-e2ab9c5-dispatch.json shows). The desk takes the 40 lowercase hex characters straight after `deploy ` at the
      start of `display_title`;
    - when that cannot be read (another title, a short or missing sha, another workflow), the row
      says "Can't check this deploy yet", with the reason "the deploy's commit isn't readable from
      its title" one tap away.
  - **The run's title, from 2026-10-17** (the desk follow-ups):
    - **Why it changes:** since the merge setting changed, a merge commit's message is the pull
      request's title and whole description ("Facts relied on"). Until Setup CS14, a push run's
      title holds that whole message. AC52's Deploys row names a run by GitHub's run `name`,
      which is its title (src/lib/sandbox.js:416, from src/lib/records.js:810), so the row would
      show the whole description, run together.
    - **From CS14:** a push run's title is `deploy <sha>`, and a hand-started run's stays
      `deploy <sha> — <note>`.
    - **The parse holds for both:** each starts `deploy ` and the 40 hex characters, then ends
      or goes on with ` — `, which the parse allows (src/lib/feed.js:766). The desk reads the
      sha from the title only for a hand-started run; a push run's comes from `head_sha`, as
      above. The production job's preview rule reads the title too
      (.github/scripts/desk_preview_check.py:28, `^deploy ([0-9a-f]{40})\b`, used at
      desk-deploy.yml:132). It also matches both forms, so CS14 must keep a title that starts
      `deploy <sha>` (plan review round 1 of the desk follow-ups, N4).
    - **What the row shows for a push deploy:** "deploy <sha>: waiting for approval", with its
      run number, linked to the run. Under it is this criterion's line, which names the pull
      request: "Matches PR #<n>'s merge · Reviewer PASS", or another line below.
    - **No desk code changes for it.** A push run started before CS14 keeps its long title until
      the owner approves or rejects it. Its check is unchanged, since it is read from `head_sha`.
  - **The check**, from records the desk reads:
    1. the pull request whose merge commit is that sha: J12's `mergeCommit` of a merged pull
       request into the default branch (J12 adds the field);
    2. that pull request's `reviews/<n>/reviewer.md` on the default branch, decided by
       reviews/README.md's rule (the first `Verdict:` at column 0).
  - **What the row says** (as drawn):
    - both hold and the verdict is PASS: "Matches PR #<n>'s merge · Reviewer PASS", with the source
      on its own line, "reviews/<n>/reviewer.md · the merge commit on <default branch>", each
      linked by AC51's link rule;
    - otherwise: "Doesn't match a reviewed pull request: don't approve", with the reason on its own
      line: "no merge of a passed pull request has this commit" when no pull request's merge commit
      is the sha, "PR #<n>'s Reviewer verdict is FAIL" or "PR #<n> has no Reviewer verdict on
      <default branch>";
    - when a read it needs has failed or not yet arrived (J12, the tree, or the verdict's blob):
      "Can't check this deploy yet", with the reason one tap away (AC41). Never a pass by default.
      In particular (build review round 1, B1 and N6b), whenever J12's kept list is not current
      for the current head: a J12 failure is set, the first-page read at the current head has not
      answered, or a cold read is under way. A pull request outside the newest 100 that was kept
      as open and merged later is settled by the daily cold read (J12); until then the kept list
      may lack its merge, and the cases above cover the time it is being read.
  - **The desk only says.** It holds no write credential (mechanism): the row's link opens the run
    on GitHub, where the owner approves, as today. The row adds no colour: a "don't approve" row
    is marked by its words and a ✕ mark (AC42), and the Deploys group's own mark follows AC66.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC72` uses J1's and J12's fixtures with a waiting deploy run
    (NOT a real record) on a head that is PR #77's merge commit with `reviews/77/reviewer.md`
    reading PASS; the same with a FAIL verdict and with no verdict; a head that is no pull
    request's merge commit; and J12's read failed, giving "Can't check this deploy yet". From
    draft 5 (B1) it adds a hand-started run (`workflow_dispatch`) whose `head_sha` is a
    records-only commit on main and whose `display_title` names PR #77's merge commit
    (`deploy <sha> — …`, its `inputs.sha` differing from `head_sha`), giving "Matches PR #77's
    merge · Reviewer PASS"; the same run with a `display_title` that names no full sha, giving
    "Can't check this deploy yet"; and a push run checked by its `head_sha`. From 2026-10-17 (the
    desk follow-ups) the push run's title is `deploy <sha>` alone, as from Setup CS14. The fixture
    sets both its `name` and its `display_title` to it, as GitHub gives them, since the row is
    built from `name` (plan review round 1 of the desk follow-ups, N8). Its row reads "deploy
    <sha>: waiting for approval" with "Matches PR #77's merge · Reviewer PASS"
    under it. The hand-started run keeps `deploy <sha> — <note>`. It checks each row's words,
    source and links, and that no row offers an approval of its own.

    storage under the key `desk-board-marks-v1`, each mark by its AC73 key, the step it was made on
    and the pull request's head then, with its time, every read and write wrapped as J5's are, so a

  - **Confirming, per step, from reads the page already makes, at their own cadence** (A3, AC14;
    "The check is intended to then confirm - at whatever cadence - is currently capable"):

    | The step | Confirmed when | The read, and its cadence |
    |---|---|---|
    | merge | the pull request is no longer in the open list | J1's open-pull-request list, in every poll (60 s) |
    | verdict | the pull request's changed files at its current head hold `reviews/<n>/owner.md`, added or modified | J20's file read, made again on each head change (the verdict's commit is one), in the blob call |
    | answer, v3 question | `decisions/questions/<name>.md` is on the default branch, or an open pull request adds it (AC77's "being recorded") | the tree, on each head change (J2); J20 for the open pull requests |
    | answer, v2.5 question | `questions/<name>.md` has gone from the default branch, or an open pull request deletes it (J20's v2.5 "being recorded") | the tree (J2); J20 |
    | answer, card or gate card | its answer file is on the default branch | the tree (J2) |
    | approve | the run is no longer `waiting`, or no longer in the lists | J1's 3a and 3b lists, in every poll |
    | open, hold card or merge card | J2 says it is no longer open | the tree and J2's reads |
    | open, a card that went missing | the card file arrives, or the state changes | the tree (J2) |
    | open, a pull request | the pull request is no longer in the open list; a new head is not a confirmation but "needs the owner again" (below) | J1's list, in every poll |

    Whatever the step, a card is also confirmed once its item no longer needs the owner by Terms'
    rule (merged, closed, answered, approved or gone). No read is added for confirming.
    - **Going to the agents is not such an end** (C; the plan review's note 10, round 1): a marked
      card whose pull request J22's rule 0 finds with the agents is neither confirmed nor kicked
      back. It leaves Done, its mark dropped, with no ✓, and is listed in the "With the agents" fold;
      once rule 0 no longer holds, it is a card in "Waiting on you" with its step then. A green ✓
      would claim GitHub showed the step done, and the agents' work says nothing of that.
    - **A mark is judged against the step it was made on** (C): if the card's step changes after the
      mark (a later "Owner verdict needed" turning a merge into a verdict), the mark still waits for
      its own step; and a kicked-back card shows its current step. After a head change, until J20
      has read the new head, the card keeps the last head's judgement (its class, its verdict),
      never falling back to "not known" for that wait (C); rule 0's "with the agents" is never kept
      so (J22).
    - **When a read counts as current:** the open list and the run lists, from this poll; the tree
      and J20's list, when their answer is for the current head (they are read again only when it
      changes, so an unmoved head's answer stays current). A read is not current when its last
      answer for the current head failed, or the page has not had one in this opening.
    - **Each poll in which the project was read successfully** (Terms), the page first confirms
      every mark it can, then judges the rest: a mark at least `KICK_BACK_MINUTES` old whose step is
      not confirmed moves its card to "Kicked back", with its reason on the card, and the card
      counts again, everywhere it counted before. Every mark, whether made in this opening or before
      it, is judged the same way, and only in such a poll. `KICK_BACK_MINUTES` is 5
      (P-001-board-bounce.md: "after about 5 minutes"), a setting to tune (C), one constant in the
      page's code.
    - **The reasons:** "GitHub doesn't show it merged yet"; "GitHub doesn't show
      reviews/<n>/owner.md on the branch yet"; "GitHub shows no answer file, or pull request for
      one, yet"; "The deploy run is still waiting" (version 5's four); and, not drawn (C), "GitHub
      shows no answer file yet" for a card, "The governance run is still not green" for a hold card,
      "The merge card is still open", "The card file still isn't there", "The pull request is still
      open as it was", and, when the read the step needs is not current, "GitHub couldn't be checked
      yet" (the safe side: it counts again).
    - **A read a mark waits on is asked again at the next poll** (C; plan review F, rounds 1 and 2,
      the Orchestrator's ruling): while a mark waits on J20's read of a pull request head that
      failed, that read is asked at each poll, not after J20's usual retry wait, **until it answers,
      at most 5 polls for that head, whoever waits on it** (draft 4, the Orchestrator's ruling on
      plan review note 3 and Critic T: every mark that waits on that head, a question's mark waiting
      on several pull requests, a re-mark from "Kicked back" and an "Undo" and mark again included,
      shares the same 5). It rides alone in a blob call of its own, so its pages 2 and 3 have that
      call's whole budget of 25 (no change to the function). After that bound, and for a kicked-back
      card, the head is read only at the existing cadence (J20's own retry), never as an extra call.
      So each pull request head costs at most 5 such calls (A3, AC14), and these solo calls count
      outside `MAX_BLOB_CALLS_PER_CYCLE` (A3).
      **The 5 hold across openings, kept on the device** (C; stage 1a's build review, round 1,
      finding 3, which measured the count kept for one opening at 2,660 such calls on AC14's day,
      past A3's 1,440 and so past 10,000 in all): the polls a head has used, its waited J20 reads
      and its verdict call's retries (J22) alike, are kept in local storage under the key
      `desk-board-waits-v1`, beside the marks', by project, pull request number and head sha, every
      read and write wrapped as the marks' are. A head still waited on at a later opening goes on
      from its count, never from 0. An entry is dropped once a successful read of its project's
      open list no longer shows that head on that pull request (a new head, or the pull request
      closed or merged), so the store holds open heads only. When local storage can't be read or
      written, no waited read is made at all, since its count could not outlive the opening: the
      mark waits on J20's own retry, inside calls already counted, with "GitHub couldn't be checked
      yet" while the read is not current (above). The count is per device, as the marks are: a head
      marked on two devices may take 5 on each, and A3's worst case counts each of its 288 heads
      marked on one device (C).
    - **Kick-backs to expect** (told to the owner in the lead): an answer to a v2.5 question given
      in the owner's session is confirmed only when its pull request opens or the question file
      goes, which usually takes longer than 5 minutes; and a hold card waits for a governance run,
      which took about 2 to 20 minutes on 2026-10-19 (Facts relied on). Such a card is kicked back
      first, then moves to Done by itself once GitHub shows its step.
    - **From "Kicked back"** the owner can mark the card done again, by dragging or by "Done ✓",
      with a new time and a new 5 minutes; "Undo" then returns it to "Kicked back" (as version 5
      does). A kicked-back card GitHub later confirms moves to Done by itself, as does any card in
      "Waiting on you" that GitHub confirms without a mark (another device, or GitHub's own page).
    - **The item wins** (the Orchestrator's ruling on plan review C): a card in Done, confirmed or
      not, whose item needs the owner again under the same AC73 key (an answer's pull request closed
      unmerged, so AC77's hold ends; a pull request reopened), or, for a mark made on an "Open ↗"
      pull request card, a new head on that pull request (the Orchestrator's ruling on plan review
      C, round 2: the owner looked, the agents pushed, and it still waits), leaves Done, its mark
      dropped, and is a card in "Waiting on you" again, with its new step.
    - **Confirmed:** the note and "Undo" go, and the ✓ turns green, as drawn. A confirmed verdict
      brings, by what the verdict file reads (J22), the "Step 2 of 2: merge" card or the "Open ↗"
      card with "You asked for changes".
    - A kicked-back card is kept on the device with its mark until its item no longer needs the
      owner, then dropped (C).

*From the owner's ruling decisions/questions/P-001-redesign-direction-v2.md ("Ruling: A — desk
mockup v2, with Home, is the direction for the whole desk: planned this way, the board first,
through the usual checks and build, in the trial view; the Design reviewer measures "sized like

("the README" below; "frame" means one of its frames). Each criterion names the frames it carries
out. Where a frame and a ruling made after d2afcfc differ, the ruling governs (the rulebook, "The
redesign direction"); a point no frame draws keeps the criteria and standing rulings that cover it.

- AC90 [trace: V4 → AC90] — When the same "not yet" reason would repeat on several rows of one
  group or phase, on Plan, the Timeline, Home or the Team screen, then it is said once, at that
  group's or phase's head, with how many rows it covers, and each row shows only what is its own.
  - The ruling: "Ruling: A — a repeated "not yet" reason on Plan, the Timeline, Home and Team is said
    once per group or phase, not on every row" (decisions/questions/P-001-audit-repeat.md, line 1);
    the option as put: "Said once at the group head, e.g. '6 milestones · no estimates yet'. Cuts
    about half of Plan's length." The audit counted the repeats: 21 rows on Plan, 15 on the
    Timeline, 3 on Home and 5 on Team (docs/design/audit-2026-10-22.md, section 4, item 1). It
    extends P-001-why-line.md's rule ("where no standard milestone's why is written yet, the phase's
    list says so once") to these screens.
  - **The rule:** a reason that two or more rows of one group would each show, word for word, is
    said once at the group's head, with the count it covers: "<n> <rows> · <reason>" when it covers
    every row, as the ruling's "6 milestones · no estimates yet", and "<k> of <n> <rows> · <reason>"
    otherwise. Each row it covers drops it. A row whose reason differs keeps its own. A gap the
    agents fill is said in their grey and still says who fills it (AC69). A group with no shared
    reason has no such line. A row's own sheet still says its state in full, since a sheet is one
    row.
  - **Where:**
    - **Plan** (AC86, AC24): in each project's group, "Estimate: not made yet" is said once, "<n>
      milestones · no estimates yet"; and a rough finish not available for one shared reason, such
      as "<code> has no estimate yet", once, "<k> rough finishes not available: <code> has no
      estimate yet". Each row shows its rough finish only once there is one;
    - **the Timeline** (AC84, AC59): in each phase run, "Why not recorded yet · for the agents to
      add" is said once under its band, "Why not recorded yet for <k> of <n> milestones · for the
      agents to add"; each milestone shows "Why <…>" only once it has one;
    - **Home** (AC82): in each group of tiles, "why it went back: not recorded" is said once at the
      group's head, "<k> projects · why their run went back: not recorded"; each such tile's Now
      line keeps its own "went back on <date>" where its record gives the date;
    - **the Team screen** (AC67, AC49): among the members' cards, and in the opened idle list,
      "not recorded in what the desk reads" is said once at the list's head, "<k> members · last
      work not recorded in what the desk reads"; each card shows "last:" only when a record names
      it.
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC90` renders Plan, the Timeline, Home and the Team screen from
    the fixtures the audit used (`service-desk/`, `poom/`, `md-extremes/`) and made-up cases
    (labelled NOT real), and checks: each shared reason said once per group with its count and its
    singular; none on the rows it covers; a row with its own reason keeping it; who fills each gap;
    no head line where no reason is shared; and a row's sheet unchanged. AC24's, AC59's, AC82's,
    AC84's, AC86's and AC67's cases that it changes are each named in the pull request and
    rewritten, never dropped (the brief). Stage 3 of "After MD3".

### N — Notifications the moment anything waits on you (first, from 2026-10-18)
*Covers AC45 as ruled on 2026-10-08 and widened by the owner's request of 2026-10-18 ("Notifications
the moment anything waits on you", draft 6), and the owner's cost instruction of 2026-10-18 (AC78).
Built first, ahead of M3A and of MD3's remaining work, in the desk as accepted, so it does not wait
for the trial view. Its senders are Workflows 3 and 4; its joins are J16 to J21; its experiment is
EXP-006. Not a milestone.*

- AC73 [trace: V1 → AC73] — When anything in a connected project, v3 or v2.5, starts waiting on
  the owner, then that project's sender counts it as waiting from the moment its record says so,
  by exactly the kinds below and no others: everything the desk counts as needing the owner
  (Terms, which from 2026-10-18 includes a waiting deploy in a project marked `deploysNeedOwner`,
  AC52, and from 2026-10-19 leaves out the pull requests the asks-merge job may still merge, AC79,
  as the owner's ruling, decisions/questions/P-001-notify-job-merges.md, already did for
  notifications), less a question being asked in a session or whose answer is being recorded
  (AC77).
  - **Changed by AC80 (with the agents, 2026-10-20):** the desk no longer counts a pull request with
    the agents (J22's rule 0: waiting on a reviewer's verdict or on the agents' fixes;
    P-001-board-after-agents.md and P-001-domain-review-count.md, both A), so neither does the
    sender: its set leaves such a pull request out, judged by the same pure rule in a module under
    `src/lib/` shared with the page, as AC79's judgment is (J16; Setup CS24), with the same verdict
    reader (`verdictOf`) and the owner check read for the same heads (`ownerCheckHeads`; draft 3,
    the Critic's note 7 and the plan review's note 4, round 2). When rule 0 stops
    holding, the pull request starts waiting and notifies, as anything newly waiting does. The
    table's pull request row is read with that exception.
  - **The kinds** (each read as J2, J9 and J16 read it, on the project's default branch):

    | Kind (the words used) | Model | Its record | It starts waiting when | It stops when |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | a decision card | v3 | `queue/<item>-<gate>-<n>.md`, gate not `dor`, `criteria` or `launch` (J2) | the card file is on the default branch with no answer `decisions/<item>/<gate>-<n>.md` | its answer is there |
    | a gate ruling | v3 | the same, gate `dor`, `criteria` or `launch` (AC52) | as a decision card | as a decision card |
    | a held loop | v3 | a hold card `queue/ci-hold-<sha12>.md`, open by J2's rule (AC46) | it is on the default branch and open: the Orchestrator writes it after holding for over 60 minutes (Terms) | J2 says it is no longer open |
    | a merge to do by hand | v3 | a merge card `queue/<item>-merge-conflict.md` or `-merge-by-hand.md`, open by J2's rule (AC47) | as a held loop | as a held loop |
    | a card that went missing | v3 | `status/<item>.toml` in state `waiting-owner` with no card file (Terms) | that state is on the default branch with no card file | the card file arrives (then it is a card, under its own key) or the state changes |
    | a question | both | `questions/<name>.md`, not `_TEMPLATE.md` (Terms, AC3) | the file is on the default branch (v3: with no answer record), unless AC77 holds it; then when AC77's hold ends | v3: its answer is on the default branch, or an open pull request adds it (AC77); both: the file is gone |
    | a pull request to merge | both | an open, non-draft pull request into the default branch, not from an `item/` branch in a v3 project (Terms, AC2) | it is opened, reopened or marked ready; for a job candidate, when J16's rule says the job has left it | it is merged, closed or turned back into a draft |
    | a deploy to approve | v3, `deploysNeedOwner` only | a workflow run in the project whose `status` is `waiting` (AC52's Deploys, J1, J16) | the run turns `waiting` | it is approved, rejected or cancelled |

  - **Not counted, so never notified:**
    - **the asks-merge job's pull requests** while the job may still merge them (J16), as ruled.
      The question such a pull request files counts once it is on the default branch: that is a
      real ask;

  - **How soon** (stated honestly; E, measured by EXP-006):
    - **in Service-Desk, on an event** (a change landing on the default branch, by the owner, the
      Orchestrator or the asks-merge job; a pull request from the project's own branches opened,
      reopened or given a new head, which starts governance and pr-body runs; a pull request marked
      ready, turned back to draft or closed, which starts the no-secret ready workflow; a check
      finishing; a deploy requested): its sender runs when that event's run completes (Workflow
      3). GitHub usually starts it within a minute (not
      documented, C); the run takes under a minute (E); Apple's delivery time is not documented.
      So usually within about 2 to 5 minutes of the record, the governance run's own length
      included;
    - **a card or a held loop** arrives with the Orchestrator's push at the end of its run's
      commit job, so it notifies when that run finishes, a minute or two after the push (E);
    - **a job candidate the asks-merge job leaves** (J16): when the first asks-merge run after its
      checks finish has judged and left it, usually within a minute or two of its last check
      (Workflow 3 admits asks-merge's own `workflow_run`-started runs, review round 3, N2); when
      that run is the job's 15-minute fallback, up to about 15 minutes; when the job's reason is
      one it would retry and it lasts (a merge conflict, a file it cannot read as text), 15 to
      about 30 minutes, the time J16's rule (b) waits to see it again;
    - **a pull request from a fork:** the origin gate (Workflow 3) skips runs a fork's pull

      run a schedule late (high load includes the start of every hour) or drop it (F-gh-12,
      F-gh-12b);

    - **in Personal-Org-Operating-Model,** its own sender (Workflow 4) runs on its pushes to main

- AC76 [trace: V1 → AC76] — When a push fails, the subscription has expired, a project or the
  sender's state can't be read, then nothing that waits is lost or sent twice on that account, and
  the owner is told on GitHub when notifications have stopped for any reason the sender can see;
  a sender that cannot run at all is a known limit, below, and so is a gone subscription that
  only the cost push has seen, which waits for the next item's push (draft 8).
  - **A push refused for now** (429, or a 5xx; Q-011 V7): retried in the same run after 5 and 30
    seconds (C); still failing, it is not marked sent, so the next run sends it again. One unsent
    for 6 hours is given up, the 6 hours counted from its first try-later or unnamed failure, never
    from a time it was kept unsent for a gone subscription or a refused sender (draft 9, build
    review round 1, Sec 2), and counted in the issue below by project and number only (C), for as
    long as it still waits. The give-up is for these answers, and for an answer this list does not
    name (draft 6; C); never for an item kept unsent because the subscription is gone or the sender
    is refused (below), which waits, unsent, until sending resumes, so nothing is lost.
  - **The subscription is gone or invalid** (410, the subscription expired; 404, which Apple gives
    for an invalid `:path`, an endpoint that is no longer right; Apple's page, Facts relied on;
    V7): the sender opens one issue in its own
    repository, or updates the open one, titled "Desk notifications have stopped", labelled
    `desk-notify`, assigned to the owner, saying why in plain words and giving Setup N5, N6 and N8's
    steps. It sends nothing more until `DESK_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION` changes (J18 keeps its keyed
    hash), then resumes, sends "Notifications are back on" (titled with the project's name, opening
    Home; draft 6, C), and closes the issue.
  - **The push service refuses the sender** (400, 401 or 403; Apple's page: "403 There's an
    error with your authentication", with a JSON `reason`): the same issue, saying why in plain
    words, and the sender keeps the item unsent and tries again each run. It mints a new JWT only
    when Apple's `reason` is `BadJwtToken` and its JWT was minted 60 minutes ago or more, never
    more often ("Don't refresh your JWT more frequently than once per hour", Apple's page); for
    `VapidPkHashMismatch` or any other reason it mints nothing and the issue says so (C). The
    first step checks that `DESK_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`'s public half equals J7's `vapidPublicKey`,
    and stops with the issue "the notification keys don't match" if not (J17). `test: fail`
    sends exactly one request, never retried and never re-minted (J17).
  - **A project unread** (its checkout or a REST read failing): its set is kept as the last run had
    it (J18), so nothing re-notifies; things that started waiting meanwhile are sent once it reads
    again. Unread for 30 minutes in a row (C), the issue says "Desk notifications can't read
    <project>", and closes once it reads again.
  - **The sender's state unreadable** (the artifact list or download failing, or the signature not
    matching, J18): the run sends nothing and uploads nothing, so the next run uses the last good
    state. A signature that does not match opens the issue at once ("the sender's memory could not
    be trusted"); a failed read, after 30 minutes in a row (C), counted from the first of the
    sender's own runs after the newest one that saved a state (draft 6; those runs saved nothing).
    When no run can be dated, because the sender's list of its own runs fails or the artifact list
    for a run fails, the run dates the failure with a second read:
    `actions/artifacts?name=desk-notify-state&per_page=100`, newest first, one page, as J18's
    fallback lists them. To each artifact's `workflow_run` it applies the checks of J18's that the
    list itself carries: `head_branch` `main`, and `repository_id` and `head_repository_id` both
    this repository's id (the runner's `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_ID`). It passes over any artifact that
    fails them, reads no run by id, and takes the newest that passes (draft 7, Critic round 5,
    finding 1: so a branch's or a fork's artifact can never keep the issue shut). The list does not
    carry the workflow's path, so a same-named artifact from another workflow on main would pass;
    only a change reviewed onto main can add one (C). If the one taken is 30 minutes old or more,
    the issue opens as for any other failed read; if the second read also fails, or its page has
    none that passes (or the repository's id is missing), the issue opens at once. The state is
    still "unreadable" either way: the run sends nothing and uploads nothing. If the issue itself
    can't be opened, the run logs it and exits as now (draft 6, the Orchestrator's settling; C).
  - **The memory issues' words, and when they close** (draft 7, Critic round 5, note 8; C):
    - a failed read for 30 minutes or more: "The sender's memory could not be read for 30 minutes
      or more, so it sends nothing until it can.";
    - at once: "The sender's memory could not be read, and GitHub didn't say for how long, so it
      sends nothing until it can. If this was a passing GitHub failure, this closes by itself.";
    - a forged state: "The sender's memory could not be trusted: its saved state's signature does
      not match, so the sender sends nothing until a good state is read.".

    Each is one line of AC76's issue, and goes at the first run whose lookup reads a state that
    verifies (J18's HMAC and limits; draft 8), or answers with none ("no state", J18), the issue
    closing when no other line is left. So an
    issue opened at once by a passing failure, the first runs' included, closes at the next run
    whose list answers.
  - **A gone subscription seen only by the cost push** (draft 7, Critic round 5, note 9; a known
    limit): AC78's cost push changes nothing else in its run, so a 410 or 404 that it alone
    receives is not reported until the next item's push meets it. Nothing that waits is lost, but
    the issue opens late, and with nothing waiting it may not open at all. The reason is privacy:
    an issue or log line the cost push caused would show a $50 crossing in Service-Desk's public
    issues and logs (AC78).
  - **An unreadable-state run rewrites the issue** (draft 9, build review round 1, Sec 6; a known
    limit): a run whose state is unreadable knows only its memory line, so it writes the issue with
    that line alone, and lines such as "subscription gone" or "refused" disappear from it until a
    run reads a state that verifies and writes them again. During a long GitHub artifact outage the
    owner can lose sight of a gone subscription, though nothing that waits is lost.
  - **The sender can't run at all** (Actions down, the workflow disabled, the switch off, 60 days
    with no activity in a public repository disabling its schedule, F-gh-12b, or the account's
    Actions minutes used up for the private project, Workflow 4): a known limit.
    Nothing on the phone says so; the desk shows everything when opened (AC1 to AC7), and GitHub's
    own failure notice for a failed run is the only signal (C).
  - **Nothing private in public places.** Service-Desk is public. Its sender reads only Service-Desk
    (Workflow 3), whose records are public already; the operating-model project's sender runs in
    that private repository (Workflow 4), with its state, logs and issues there. Even so, every
    key a sender stores is a keyed hash (J18), every issue names projects and counts only, every
    log line holds counts, reasons and keyed hashes only, no usage figure appears in a log, an
    issue or the state in clear (AC78), and no fixture copies a file of the private project
    (AC73).
  - A test marked `ac-test: S-001/AC76` drives the sender with a fake push service answering 201,
    429 then 201, 503 three times, 404, 410, 403 `BadJwtToken` then 201 after a new JWT, 403
    `BadJwtToken` over five runs in one hour (one new JWT only), 403 `VapidPkHashMismatch` (no new

  asked in ends or the answer's pull request opens; and when the owner taps any answer link, the desk first makes sure

    <n>"; and this criterion's re-read before an answer link runs before every board answer button
    (AC80). The holds, the reads and the sender are unchanged. Its test's sandbox cases
    (tests/desk/notify-ac77-desk.test.mjs, the Merges and Decisions rows) follow the board.

    landing with this spec's pull request): "the question that came through here, that I answered,
    lingered in the service desk as a decision - with the option to merge in GitHub. Thinking it
    was a legit option I went through that path but it was stale". The windows the records show,

    (decisions/questions/P-001-file-only-required.md, line 1).
  - **Being asked** (from the moment it is on the default branch; C): the Chief of Staff writes, in
    a question it asks in a session, one line in column 0, `Asked in session: <session id>`
    (J13's id form, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}`): in a v3 question, the line directly after its
    `Milestone:` line; in a v2.5 question (no `Milestone:` line, J2), the first line after its
    `# Ruling needed:` line that is not blank (J2, CS17). The model's checks allow it as they

      its piece's start line at 11:26:22Z). A start line ends nothing either. While the page has

      side; the 8-hour fallback below still runs). Once such an end line is there, the piece is over, so the question becomes an ordinary waiting one, with its link,
      and the sender notifies it;
    - **8 hours after its raised time** (AC20's; while that read has not arrived, the time this
      device first saw it), a fallback only (C: J13's own limit for a piece of work with no end

      - **A failed read** (finding 2c, 2d): on the page, the closed read, a found pull request's

- AC78 [trace: V3 → AC78] — When the owner looks at the desk, then it shows the owner's GitHub
  account's Actions use this billing period as a percent bar of the plan's included minutes, and,
  once use is past them, an estimated cost so far, labelled an estimate; and each time that
  estimate crosses a new $50 step, the owner's iPhone shows one notification, once per step per
  billing period. Where GitHub does not report the account's Actions use to the desk, the desk
  says so plainly, with no bar and no $50 notifications. Nothing about cost asks the owner to
  approve anything.
  - **Why** (the owner's instruction of 2026-10-18, docs/design/references/owner-github-plan-2026-10-18.md,
    762e93f): "I’m not concerned about the pricing to the point I want to approve things
    constantly. For the time being I simply want an action count, shown as a percent bar of some
    sort. Once the actions begin to surpass my allotted amount, I want an estimation of cost and a
    notification at $50 increments." "Action count" is read as Actions minutes, the unit GitHub's
    included use and its prices are counted in (the record's own reading: "the desk shows the
    account's Actions use as a percent bar of the included minutes"; C). Its basis is that
    instruction, not a value target; it is traced to V3 (owner upkeep, tokens included,
    PROJECT.md §6) because that is the target it touches both ways (C): the owner needs no time on
    billing pages to know where the account stands, and it adds one token to renew (Setup N12,
    about 5 minutes at each expiry, counted in V3's 30 minutes a week). It is a stated exception to
    "Spend: out of the first version" ("What this spec does not cover"): it shows the account's
    GitHub Actions cost only, on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-18, and no other spend
    (Critic round 4, note 9).
  - **Where it reads from** (J21; research Q-015, source-checked: FAIL on F1.5 only, its
    conditions taken, research/Q-015-source-check.md; CS19): GitHub's billing usage endpoints for
    a user, `GET /users/<account>/settings/billing/usage/summary` and `GET
    /users/<account>/settings/billing/usage`, with `year` and `month` always given (Q-015 F1.1,
    F1.2, U-9; the summary's `month` "Default value is the current month", and a tutorial says the
    summaries default to the current year, so both are always passed). The old
    `/users/<account>/settings/billing/actions` is never used: it is absent from GitHub's REST
    data (F1.8, A; the 2025-09-25/26 announcement of its closing, F1.7, is unverified and not
    relied on). `<account>` is J7's `actionsUsage.account`, `shumpmaster`.
  - **Whether GitHub reports it at all** (draft 5; Q-015's source check, F1.5; a new unknown,
    U-11): GitHub's REST usage page says user endpoints "are only applicable if the user has
    purchased their own Copilot plan" (github/docs commit 9c32d33, 2026-01-22), while the same
    reference's examples are Actions items and the migration page moved Actions reporting to
    `/usage`. So for a Pro account with no Copilot plan these endpoints may give no Actions data,
    or refuse. UNKNOWN; EXP-006 case 11's first call settles it, with U-1. If they do not report
    it, the desk falls back as below ("Not reported").
  - **The billing period** (Q-015 F3.1, F3.2, A): the calendar month in UTC, from 00:00:00 UTC on
    the 1st; the included minutes reset then. The desk names the month ("October") and, under the
    bar, "Resets at the start of each month (UTC): <next month's 1st, 00:00 UTC, in
    ownerTimeZone, as J9's `<t>`>". The included minutes are J7's `actionsUsage.includedMinutes`, 3,000 for Pro (Facts
    relied on; Q-015 F3.4).
  - **The bar** (C): one line, "GitHub Actions this month", in More detail in both views, beside
    "Notifications" (AC75), and nowhere else: on the accepted page, in AC75's "More detail" fold at
    the bottom of Home (draft 8; the owner's ruling "A. Keep the fold (Recommended)",
    decisions/questions/P-001-notify-more-detail.md, pull request #112, with the screenshots
    docs/design/mockups/notify-more-detail/ on the branch orch/s001-notifications); a
    notification's tap opens More detail, the fold included, at it (`/?open=actions-usage`).
    - It reads "<m> of <n> included minutes (<p>%)", with a bar filled to `min(p, 100)`%, as an
      element with `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 100 and `aria-valuenow`
      `min(p, 100)`, its words always shown, never colour alone. `p` is `floor(100 × m ÷ n)`.
    - `<m>` is the month's minutes in the account's private repositories: the sum of `quantity`
      over J21's `/usage` items whose `product` is `Actions` (any letter case) and `unitType`
      `minutes`, less those whose `repositoryName` names one of the account's public repositories
      (J21), since public repositories' minutes are free and use none of the included minutes but
      may sit in the totals (Q-015 F3.5, F5.2). An item with no `repositoryName` is counted (C).
      **How far off that can be** (Critic round 4, note 8): `/usage` gives only summarised data
      (Q-015 F1.6), so the field may be absent on every item; then the bar also counts
      Service-Desk's free minutes, its sender alone about 288 runs a day, roughly 9,000 minutes a
      month, and would read "past your included minutes" when private use is under 3,000. So when
      any Actions minutes item lacks `repositoryName`, the line adds "(GitHub didn't name the
      repository for some minutes, so this may be too high)". The estimate is not affected: it
      comes from `netAmount`. And whether `/usage` pages its results is not documented, so an
      unseen page would under-count. EXP-006 case 11 measures both against GitHub's billing page.
      Minutes are counted as GitHub reports them, whatever the runner (whether other runners still
      draw down the allowance at a multiple is Q-015 U-4).
    - If the month's `netAmount` on standard runners' minute items (a `sku` naming Linux, Windows
      or macOS, in either form, Q-015 F1.4) is above 0, `p` is at least 100 (C, from Q-015 F5.2,
      itself C; Critic round 4, note 7): with standard runners a charge means the included minutes
      are used up. Larger runners are always charged (F3.5), so their items are left out of this
      rule.
    - Past 100%, the bar is full, the words say "<m> minutes: past your <n> included minutes
      (<p>%)", and the estimate shows under it.
  - **The estimate** (C): "Estimated cost so far this month: $<x.xx>", then "an estimate from
    GitHub's usage figures, which may lag; GitHub bills the final amount on your billing date"
    (Q-015 F3.1, U-3). It shows whenever it is above $0.00, which happens only once included use
    is spent or for something the allowance does not cover.
    - `<x>` is the sum of `netAmount` over the summary's `usageItems` whose `product` is `Actions`
      (any letter case), all its SKUs, minutes and storage alike, as the bill counts them (Q-015
      F1.2, F5.1, F5.2). `netAmount` is already net of the included use (gross less discount), so
      the included minutes are never subtracted again.
    - If the summary does not answer in that form (it is still labelled preview, Q-015 F1.2,
      F1.3), the sum of `netAmount` over `/usage`'s Actions items is used instead, and the line adds
      "(from the daily report)".
    - An item lacking `netAmount` is priced as `quantity` (or the summary's `netQuantity`) ×
      `pricePerUnit` from the same item; lacking that too, a Linux minutes item (`sku` naming Linux,
      in either form, Q-015 F1.4) at $0.006 a minute, GitHub's price for standard Linux 2-core
      runners from 2026-01-01 (Q-015 F4.1, F4.2), and the line adds "(some prices assumed)"; any
      other item lacking both is left out and the estimate reads "at least $<x.xx>". No other price

    once an hour while that opening stays open, and again on a tap from a cost notification. It
    keeps the figures in the page's memory only, so each opening reads afresh and nothing is
    stored on the device (J21).

    - the token refused (401 or 403), or 404 from both endpoints: "GitHub Actions use: can't be
      read: the usage token was refused, or GitHub doesn't report Actions use for this account"

      now";

  - **Not reported** (draft 5; C): when GitHub reports no Actions use to the desk for this
    account, the line reads "GitHub doesn't report Actions use to the desk for this account. Turn

    no estimate and no $50 notification, and the sender opens no issue for it. It shows:

      fix-forward pull request when case 11 finds no Actions data, or a refusal with both token
      kinds (Setup N12 step 4); then neither the page nor the sender reads the endpoints;
    - and, while `reported` is not `false`, when both endpoints answer 200 with no Actions item
      for the month on any day but the month's 1st (UTC); on the 1st, an empty answer reads "0 of
      <n> included minutes (0%)", since the month has just begun.
    In that case Setup N11 is recommended, not optional.
  - **The $50 notifications** (Workflow 3's sender only, J21; C):
    - the sender reads the same figures at most once an hour, in a run whose state (J18) shows the
      last usage read 60 minutes ago or more, so about hourly, since Workflow 3 runs at least every
      5 minutes; only the project whose J7 entry holds `actionsUsage`, Service-Desk, reads them
      (draft 9, build review round 1, Sec 5), so Workflow 4, running the same code and J7 for its
      own project, never reads them, whatever secrets it holds;
    - the step is `floor(x ÷ 50)` for the month's estimate `x`, as above; when it is above the last
      step notified for the same UTC year and month (kept in J18's state, encrypted), the sender
      sends one notification and records the new step; several steps crossed between two reads
      give one notification, naming the highest;
    - its words: title "Service Desk", body "GitHub Actions: this month's estimated cost has passed
      $<50 × step> (about $<x.xx>, an estimate)"; its tap opens `<deskUrl>/?open=actions-usage`;
      its `Topic` and `tag` are J17's, from the key `account|actions-cost|<yyyy-mm>|<step>`;
    - a new UTC month starts at step 0, so the first $50 of each month notifies again;
    - **the first run with no state** (J18's bootstrap) records the month's current step as sent
      and, when the estimate is above $0.00, its summary adds "GitHub Actions: about $<x.xx> so far
      this month (an estimate)", so turning notifications on mid-month gives no burst; a state
      lost after 7 days without a run does the same, so a step crossed in that gap is shown in the
      summary, not notified on its own (a known limit);
    - **a state with no usage part** (draft 5, Critic round 4, note 5): in the real order the state
      exists from N7 and N8, before the token (N12), so this is the usual start. At the first
      successful usage read, the sender records the month's step and, if it is 1 or more, sends one
      cost notification naming the highest step passed, so the owner learns where the month stands
      once; at step 0 it sends nothing;
    - this is the one notification that does not mean something waits on the owner: it is not in
      AC73's set, the desk counts nothing for it, it never stops "Quiet", and it is always sent on
      its own, never folded into AC74's grouped notification. The owner asked for it;
    - a usage read that fails keeps the last step and sends nothing; unread for 24 hours in a row,
      or refused (401 or 403) at once, AC76's issue says "GitHub Actions use can't be read: <the
      reason>", and closes once it reads again;
    - no figure is ever in a log line, an issue or the state in clear: Service-Desk's logs, issues

      review round 1, Sec 3), and its answer changes nothing else: not the subscription's or the
      refusal's state, nor the issue; a gone or refused subscription shows on the next item's push;
  - **GitHub's own alerts, a complement:** GitHub e-mails at 90% and 100% of included use when the
    owner turns that on (Setup N11), and budgets e-mail at 75%, 90% and 100% of a dollar amount;

    GitHub reports the use; where it does not ("Not reported"), those e-mails are what is left, and
    N11 is recommended.
  - **What to expect** (E): at $0.006 a minute a $50 step needs about 8,300 charged minutes in a
    month; at the rate counted from run times in round 3 (about 7,500 minutes a month in all, so
    about 4,500 charged, about $27; plan review round 4), no $50 notification may come in a month,
