      review_check's checked-out tree also holds) counts too, read from the checkout with no
      request, by the same reader, unless the list shows it `removed` (J22). This holds for a v3 and
      a v2.5 project alike (settled after MD3; stage 1b's review, round 1, reading 2); for a v2.5
      project the page counts such a file as given, unread, so the two sides can differ (Known
      limits, after MD3, 1). **A blob is read
      once:** J18 keeps each verdict read by its blob sha, so a later run, at the same head or a new
      one holding the same file, reads nothing for it; a blob sha names the file's contents, so a
      kept verdict never outlives what it read. The owner's own verdict file, `reviews/<n>/owner.md`,
      is read the same way, once per blob sha, only for the selection below.
    - **(i), the owner check:** only where the page reads it (J22: a v3 project whose repository is
      public, `base.repo.private` `false` in J1's list), so Workflow 4, for the private v2.5
      operating-model project, never applies (i), and the board and the phone judge that project
      alike. Where it applies, it is read **for the same heads the page reads it for**: at most 3 a
      project, chosen by one function in the shared module, `ownerCheckHeads`, which the page's
      poll call uses too (J22's "The owner check's read": the open pull requests not settled by
      their owner's verdict file and not already with the agents by (ii), whatever (a) gives, in
      AC52's order, ties by the lower number; draft 4, the Critic's B1, round 3, which found draft
      3 leaving out every pull request (a) marks, where GitHub posts "Owner: after agents"), from
      the same inputs (J1's list, J20's lists, `governance/risk-paths.toml` and the verdicts read);
      a fourth or fifth head is "not read" on both sides, so (i) does not hold for it, and it is a
      card on the board and in the sender's set alike (draft 3; the Critic's note 7 and the plan
      review's note 4, round 2, which found the sender reading every head). Where the two sides'
      reads differ for a moment (a verdict one has read and the other has not yet), their choices
      can differ: a head one side has settled, or found with the agents by (ii), the other may still
      choose, and that head can push a later one out of the other side's three. The effect falls on
      the head pushed out: on that side (i) is unread for it, so it shows the card or notifies, a
      needless card or notification, never a hidden one (draft 4; the plan review's note 5, round
      3, which found draft 3 naming the wrong head). For each chosen head, its `owner-verdict` entry
      of `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status?per_page=100` is read each run as a conditional
      request with the ETag J18 keeps for that head; a 304 gives the kept answer.
    - **Read last, and skipped near the floor** (draft 4; the plan review's B1, round 3, and the
      owner's ruling, decisions/questions/P-001-desk-v2-plan-stop.md, A): the owner-check reads are
      the run's last GitHub reads, after every other read of every project and before the set is
      worked out and anything is sent: that is, the last reads on the workflow token before the set
      (settled after MD3; stage 1b's review, round 1, reading 1). AC78's usage read uses the owner's
      own token and limit (J21), and AC76's issue sync comes after sending. They are skipped, all of them, for the run when the
      `X-RateLimit-Remaining` of the run's last answer before them is below 400, the guard's floor
      of 300 plus 100 (about four quiet runs' reads, J16's 10 to 25 each), so they never use the
      last 100 before the floor, which the sender's other reads keep. When that answer carries no
      `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header (an uncredentialed download, say), they are skipped too, the
      safe reading (the confirmation check of draft 4, minor note). A skipped read is "not read":
      (i) does not hold for that head this run, so the pull request is judged as it is today, by (ii)
      and Terms' rule, and notifies if it waits (a needless notification at worst, never a hidden
      one); its kept ETag and answer stay in J18 for the next run, and the board, which reads the
      check on its own, is not affected.
    - **Never across heads:** each outcome is the current head's, from that head's reads; nothing a
      run judged at an earlier head counts at a new one (J22), but a verdict kept by its blob sha,
      which is the same file's.
    - **When a read fails** (the page's safe sides, so a pull request that needs the owner is never
      hidden, V1): a verdict blob whose read fails, is refused, answers 404, is over 1 MB, or isn't
      UTF-8 text counts as given, and is not kept, so the next run asks again. No other kind of
      answer can come: the read is by a blob sha J20's list gives for an added or modified path, so
      the contents form's directory, symlink and submodule answers never arise. An owner check whose
      read fails, is refused or is malformed is "not read", so (i) does not hold. A pull request from
      a fork is never read for files or contents and is judged by (i) alone, as on the page; so is
      one whose file list holds 300 files or more, and every pull request while the checkout's
      `governance/risk-paths.toml` is missing or can't be read (its required reviewers then
      unknown). A failed file list already makes the project's set "not read" this run (the awkward
      cases below; src/notify/collect.mjs:112-114), so no judgement rests on an unread list.
    - **Its cost** (E; draft 3, the plan review's note 5, round 2): each run, one conditional status
      read for each head `ownerCheckHeads` chooses, at most 3 a project; and one blob read per
      verdict file the first time its sha is seen, a few per verdict commit. **Whether the status
      reads come back as uncounted 304s is not known:** each run has a new `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the ETag
      J18 keeps came under an earlier run's token, and GitHub's answer carries `Vary:
      Authorization` (Facts relied on), so this spec counts every status read as a counted 200: on
      2026-10-19's runs (990 started, 262 of them ran the sender: 249 concluded `success` and 13
      `failure`; the rest skipped or cancelled, Facts relied on), 1 to 3 reads a run, so roughly 260
      to 800 counted reads a day (the plan review's bound, round 2: about 300 to 900), and at most
      about 180 in an hour of 60 runs. Draft 4's selection (the open pull requests (a) marks taken
      in) adds no head to that bound, which is per project, but more runs reach it, so the day's
      count sits nearer 800 than 260. **What this can still pause** (draft 4; the plan review's B1,
      round 3, which found draft 3's "nothing is silenced" untrue): the budget guard reads the
      token's whole remaining count, shared with the asks-merge job and the Orchestrator (above),
      and a busy hour already comes near it: J16's worst hour is about 1,500 requests, and
      2026-10-19 had 58 sender runs between 21:00 and 22:00 UTC and 41 between 17:00 and 18:00
      (Facts relied on). In such an hour these reads bring the guard's stop up to about 180
      requests sooner, fewer as the skip above takes effect, so a run that would have sent can find
      the budget under 300 and send nothing: its sends wait for the next run with budget, up to
      about an hour (AC74), with nothing lost, and the board unaffected. Draft 1's uncounted 1,700
      to 2,600 a day (the plan review's count, round 1) do not arise. A 304 that does come back
      uncounted only lowers this; nothing rests on it.
  - **The set:** AC73's kinds, each with its key. A v3 project's cards, hold cards, merge cards,
    status files, questions and answers are read as J2 reads them; a v2.5 project's questions as
    J2's owner questions read them in either model; pull requests by Terms' rule; deploys by `status` `waiting`, only where J7 marks
    the project `deploysNeedOwner`; and AC77's held and being-recorded questions left out.
  - **The asks-merge job's pull requests** (the owner's ruling,
    decisions/questions/P-001-notify-job-merges.md). In a project whose default branch holds
    `.github/workflows/asks-merge.yml` and a standing asks-merge grant in docs/LEDGER.md (a
    `type: delegation` entry whose `decision:` begins `asks-merge:` and that no later entry
    supersedes, as `find_grant` reads it, asks_merge.py:334), a pull request is a **job
    candidate** when its head branch is in the repository, its base is the default branch, and
    every path in J20's file list is one of the four kinds by path (asks_merge.py:29-38, with
    `QUESTION_RE`, `ANSWER_RE` and `SESSION_RE` at :81-83): an added `questions/<name>.md`, a
    deleted `questions/<name>.md`, an added `decisions/questions/<name>.md`, each `<name>` holding
    no `/` and not starting with `_`; or an added or changed
    `sessions/chief-of-staff/<id>.jsonl`. This mirrors the job's kinds by path only (C); its finer
    rules are left to the job itself, and seen through its runs, (b) below.
    - **A job candidate waits on the owner** from the first of these (C):
      - (a) the latest run of a counted check on its head (one per key, as `check_state` keeps
        only the latest, asks_merge.py:236-247) finishes with any conclusion but `success`, or the
        latest status of a counted context turns `failure` or `error`, counted as the job counts
        them: every check run but those of `.github/workflows/orchestrator.yml`, every status but
        `owner-questions` (asks_merge.py:74-75);
      - (b) **the job has left it** (review B2 and N8; C): every counted check on its head has
        completed with `success`, and an asks-merge run that started after the last of them
        finished (started by `workflow_run`, `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch`, and from 2026-10-19
        with its `head_branch` the default branch, so a branch's dispatch of a changed job counts
        for nothing, AC79; R3; and, from draft 5, the security build review's C, round 1, the
        Orchestrator's ruling, with its `head_sha` an ancestor of, or equal to, the checkout's
        default-branch HEAD, `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, so a dispatch on a tag named like the
        default branch counts for nothing too; from draft 6, the desk build review's R1, round 2,
        the Orchestrator's ruling, that ancestry check applies only to `workflow_dispatch` runs:
        `workflow_run` and `schedule` runs use the default branch's own workflow file, so they are
        taken as before, and a real run newer than the checkout is not held back a sender run, which
        also settles the security build review's R3, round 2) has a `merge` job
        that ran (read from the run's jobs; a run whose job was skipped or cancelled does not
        count, since asks-merge.yml:37 skips every run not caused by a pull request) and whose log
        holds the line `PR #<n>: waits: <reason>` for this pull request (the job's own words,
        asks_merge.py:632, read from the job's log, `GET
        /repos/<repo>/actions/jobs/<job id>/logs`, with `actions: read`).
        - **The log's form** (review round 3, N3; C): GitHub's job log is plain text, and each line
          starts with a timestamp, such as `2026-10-18T12:50:29.1234567Z `, before the program's own
          output. The sender takes each line's text after a leading `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT[0-9:.]+Z `
          (or the whole line when it has none) and matches `^PR #(\d+): waits: (.+)$` on that
          text. Its test reads one real asks-merge job log (CS18).
        - **The job's words, well formed** (draft 5 of the being-recorded amendment; the security
          build review's A, round 1, the Orchestrator's ruling): both sides apply this, in the
          shared judgment (`judgeCandidate`, src/lib/jobcand.js). A run's log counts as the job's
          words only when its `PR #n:` lines name each number at most once, in strictly ascending
          number order, as the job prints them (Facts relied on). A log that breaks this is judged
          as if that run printed nothing, and every candidate it names counts (the sender notifies,
          the page counts) until a later well-formed run judges it (from draft 6, a later successful
          well-formed run, below). The reason: the job prints a
          pull request's file paths unescaped in its reasons, so a pushed file name holding a line
          break could print a forged `PR #<n>: merged` line for another pull request. **Dependency
          note:** the model change that removes the cause, asks_merge.py printing paths escaped
          (`repr`) or refusing control characters in paths, is the operating model's, not this
          spec's work ("What this spec does not cover"), and it fully closes the security build
          review's A; until it lands, the successful-job rule below is the reader-side guard. This
          rule stays either way.
        - **Verdicts only from a successful job** (draft 6; the security build review's R1, round 2,
          the Orchestrator's ruling): both sides apply this, in the shared judgment. Verdicts are
          taken only from a judging run whose `merge` job concluded `success`. If the `merge` job
          completed with any other conclusion (`failure`, `timed_out` and so on, but not `skipped`
          or `cancelled`), it is the forged case: every candidate its log names counts, on both
          sides, until a later successful well-formed run judges it. A skipped or cancelled job
          judges nothing, as now. This closes the case the well-formed rule misses: a run stopped
          right after a forged line, whose log is still in ascending order.
        - **The reason, at once:** a reason the job will not clear by itself leaves the pull
          request at once: anything but a reason holding "cannot be read", one starting "it could
          not be judged" or "GitHub refused the merge" (the job skips those until its next run,
          asks_merge.py:49), "no counted check run on the head yet", or a check run or status not
          yet completed.
        - **A retried reason that lasts** (review round 3, N4; C): one of those the job retries (a
          reason holding "cannot be read", such as "cannot be read as text" for a file that is
          not text, asks_merge.py:149, one starting "it could not be judged", or "GitHub refused
          the merge", which a merge conflict gives on every run, asks_merge.py:636-641) leaves the
          pull request when a judging run whose `run_started_at` is 15 minutes or more after the
          `run_started_at` of the first judging run that gave a reason of these three for it on
          the same head gives one again. Both times are the asks-merge runs' own (draft 5, review
          round 4, N3): J18 keeps the first such run's `run_started_at` for that head, not when this
          sender read it, so the 14- and 15-minute cases have one meaning. The job's 15-minute
          schedule makes such a later run likely within 15 to 30 minutes.
        - **A known limit, against ruling A:** a GitHub outage of more than 15 minutes that gives
          "it could not be judged" on two such runs notifies a pull request the job may still
          merge once GitHub recovers; the notification then names something that soon stops
          waiting (C, rare).
        - A run that judged nothing (the open pull requests unread, no grant: `return 0` with no
          `PR #` line, asks_merge.py:609-620) does not count, and nor does a log that cannot be
          read. The pull request must still be open with the same head;
        - **Its reads, bounded** (draft 6; C, for the budget): one page of the latest 30
          asks-merge runs a run, and, per candidate, at most 5 job logs, newest run first, a run
          whose `merge` job did not run using none of the 5. An earlier retried reason's time is
          already kept in J18, so the newest judging runs are enough;
      - (c) 30 minutes with no counted check started on its head, counted from the later of the
        head commit's time and the first run of this sender that saw that head (kept in J18); a head
        commit time more than 10 minutes after the reader's clock is ignored and treated as no head
        time, on both sides (draft 5; the security build review's D, round 1, the Orchestrator's
        ruling; AC79), so a commit dated in the future can't hold rule (c) off;
      - (d) the grant no longer stands;
      - (e) (draft 6; the security build review's R2, round 2, the Orchestrator's ruling) its checks
        have all completed and no judging run has judged it within 45 minutes after that: it counts
        on both sides (the sender notifies, and the page counts with no special words, AC79). This
        bounds a stalled or broken job. The 45 minutes are a setting to tune (C), kept in the shared
        judgment. **A known limit** (draft 7; the desk build review's R2, round 3, the
        Orchestrator's ruling, option 2): if the sender can't download a job log it needs while a
        candidate has been unjudged for over 45 minutes, the phone can be told before the desk stops
        showing "Being recorded" (AC79). This lasts until the sender's next successful read. It is
        rare and short-lived. Page-side failures never cause it.

      Until then it is not in the set. A new head starts it again. A pull request that is no job
      candidate (any other path) waits from its opening, as any pull request. The sender never
      merges, and never says a pull request "will be merged".
    - In a project with no grant (Personal-Org-Operating-Model at 90f53e3 has neither the
      workflow nor a grant), no pull request is a job candidate.
  - **Awkward cases:**
    - **a read fails:** the project's set is "not read" this run, and J18 keeps its last set
      (AC76);
    - **J20 lists 300 files or more** (the job's own cap, `COMPARE_FILE_CAP`): no job candidate,
      so it waits from its opening;
    - **a candidate's head with more than 10 pages (of 100) of check runs, statuses or workflow
      runs** (draft 6; draft 7, Critic round 5, note 12: the job's own limit, `PAGES = 10`,
      asks_merge.py:79, past which its `get_pages`, :448-460, reads nothing, so the job does not
      merge it either): no job candidate, so it waits as any pull request, as for 300 files
      (rare);
    - **a record that can't be parsed:** activity, as on the desk, never in the set;
    - **a deploy run `queued` when it is requested:** read again every 15 seconds for up to 2
      minutes (C); still not `waiting`, the next run finds it;
    - **a pull request turned into a draft and back, or closed and reopened, between two runs:**
      not seen to stop, so not new (a known limit, AC73).

- **J17 — A sender → the push service → the desk on the phone (Workflows 3 and 4; added
  2026-10-18, draft 3, AC74, AC76).**
  - **The subscription:** the secret `DESK_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION`, the JSON the desk showed (J19):
    `{"endpoint": "<https URL>", "expirationTime": null, "keys": {"p256dh": "<base64url>", "auth":
    "<base64url>"}}` (V2). A value that isn't that form stops the run at its first step, naming
    the secret, never printing it.
  - **The keys' check, first** (B1's fix): the public half of `DESK_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` (a PEM of a
    P-256 key, Setup N1) must equal J7's `push.vapidPublicKey`; if not, the run stops and opens
    AC76's issue, "the notification keys don't match".
  - **VAPID** (V1; RFC 8292): a JWT signed ES256, its `aud` the endpoint's origin, its `sub` the
    secret `DESK_VAPID_SUBJECT` (`mailto:<the owner's address>`, a secret so the address is in no
    public file), sent as `Authorization: vapid t=<jwt>, k=<J7's public key>`.
    - **Refreshed at most hourly** (V8, B: Apple asks senders to refresh the JWT at most hourly)
      (C): a run mints a JWT only when the state holds none, one minted 60 minutes ago or more,
      or one whose `aud` is not the subscription's origin (a new subscription on another push
      service, since a JWT is good only for its `aud`, V1; draft 6);
      its `exp` is 2 hours after it was minted (within V1's 24 and within Apple's "more than one
      day into the future", which is a `BadJwtToken`). It is kept in J18's state, encrypted with
      AES-256-GCM under a key derived from `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`, so the public artifact does
      not expose it. Apple's page, read 2026-10-18: "Don't refresh your JWT more frequently than
      once per hour" (Facts relied on). A 403 whose `reason` is `BadJwtToken` mints a new JWT only
      if the last was minted 60 minutes ago or more (AC76). EXP-006 case 8 checks that Apple
      accepts a reused JWT.
  - **The payload,** encrypted for the subscription with `aes128gcm` (V3; RFC 8291), with Node's
    built-in crypto only, in the Declarative Web Push form (D1), which the service worker also
    reads (C): `{"web_push": 8030, "notification": {"title": "<title>", "body": "<body>",
    "navigate": "<deskUrl>/?sandbox&open=<key>", "tag": "<topic>"}}` (from 2026-10-19; AC74's
    tap), under 4,096 bytes (V4). The `tag`
    sits inside `notification`, so it reaches the phone on both paths, if Declarative Web Push
    honours it; EXP-006 case 6 checks it, and if it does not, a repeat on that path may add a
    notification rather than replace one (a known limit).
  - **Headers** (V5, V6): `TTL: 86400` (C), `Urgency: high` (C), `Topic: <topic>`, where `<topic>`
    is the first 32 characters of the base64url HMAC of the key (J18), so a resent push replaces
    one still waiting in the push service (V6); `Content-Encoding: aes128gcm`.
  - **The answers** (V7; Apple's page): `201` sent; `429` and `5xx` retried (AC76); `410` the
    subscription expired and `404` an invalid `:path`, both treated as the subscription gone;
    `400`, `401` and `403` the request or the signature refused, with Apple's JSON `reason` read
    when present (AC76, never a stop); `413` too large, sent again once with the body cut to 60 characters. The push service
    never sees the subscription's `p256dh` or `auth` (RFC 8291), so a wrong one gives 201 and a push
    the phone cannot read; the sender never sends one.
  - **The tests from GitHub:** `workflow_dispatch` with `test: true` sends "Test from your desk:
    notifications work", opening Home, every one under the key `<project>|test`, so with one
    `Topic` and `tag`, and a second replaces the first (draft 6; EXP-006 case 6 relies on it); with
    `test: fail` it makes exactly one request, a push signed with a throwaway VAPID key made in that
    run and sent as `k=`, with no retry, no new JWT
    and no other send in that run, so the push service refuses it (on Apple, 403 with a `reason`
    such as `VapidPkHashMismatch`) and nothing reaches the phone; AC76's issue opens, marked
    "(test)", and closes on the next good push (C). It never sends a push the phone cannot read
    (W8): its body, should a push service ever accept it, reads "Test from your desk: this test
    should have been refused" (draft 6; C).
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J17` covers it: the encryption against RFC 8291's worked
    example in its appendix, byte for byte, where the RFC gives one (C: the Builder confirms it;
    otherwise a round trip, decrypting with Node's crypto and the subscription's private key); the
    JWT's header, claims and an ES256 signature that verifies with the public key; minting at most
    hourly, and a new JWT after a `BadJwtToken` 403 only when an hour has passed; the keys' check;
    `test: fail` making exactly one request; the headers; the payload's form and size;
    each answer code; `test: fail` signing with a key that is not J7's; and that no log line holds
    the endpoint, a key, the JWT or the subject.

- **J18 — A sender's memory between runs (Workflows 3 and 4; added 2026-10-18, draft 3, AC74,
  AC76).** No database and no Cloudflare service, as ruled.
  - **Where** (C): one workflow artifact, `desk-notify-state`, uploaded at the end of each run that
    built a state (the upload step runs only when the program wrote the file, so a run stopped at
    its first step uploads nothing), kept 7 days.
  - **Taken only from the sender's own runs** (round 1, B3; round 2, Critic B3; research Q-014):
    a `workflow_run`-started run has `GITHUB_REF` main and runs main's file (Q-014 F1.1, F1.3, A),
    and the runs list files it under main (F1.4 and F3.1, C, observed; the REST `branch=` filter
    giving the same is F3.3, UNKNOWN, EXP-006 case 10). So the lookup does not rest on a branch
    filter. The next run lists its own workflow's runs by its file
    (`actions/workflows/desk-notify.yml/runs?status=success&per_page=100`, one page only, so the
    search is bounded: C), newest first. `status=success` lists only runs that concluded
    `success` (GitHub's REST reference for listing a workflow's runs takes a conclusion as
    `status`; C, EXP-006 case 10 checks it), so the many runs whose job the origin gate skipped,
    which conclude `skipped`, never fill the page (review round 3, N5); with `status=completed`
    as its fallback if the filter is refused. If EXP-006 case 10 finds that skipped runs conclude
    `success` too, so neither filter keeps them out (review round 4, N4), the lookup starts instead
    from the repository's artifacts by name, `actions/artifacts?name=desk-notify-state`, newest
    first, one page of 100, and applies the checks below to each artifact's `workflow_run` (its
    run read by id); a skipped run uploads nothing, so it never appears there (C). It takes the
    newest run that: has `path`
    `.github/workflows/desk-notify.yml`; has `repository` and `head_repository` this repository;
    has `head_branch` `main`; has an `event` among the workflow's own triggers; and uploaded
    `desk-notify-state`. It reads that run's artifact (`actions/runs/<id>/artifacts`), checking the
    artifact's `workflow_run` id against the run. A run or artifact that fails these checks is
    passed over and never read, so it is neither taken nor "unreadable": the lookup goes on to the
    next (draft 6; C, so a branch's or another workflow's run can neither feed the sender nor stop
    it). None in that page, with the list answering, is "no state" (below). The HMAC is the real
    guard: a run elsewhere, even one passing those checks, cannot sign without
    `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`, which only `notify` jobs hold.
  - **Signed and parsed with limits:** the state is a JSON file and an HMAC-SHA-256 of its bytes
    under `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`; a state whose HMAC does not match is not used (AC76). The zip is
    read only if under 1 MB, the JSON under 256 KB, with at most 5,000 keys, counting the waiting
    keys, the job candidates and the recorded questions together (draft 6); anything else is not
    used.
  - **What it holds:** its form version; the run's time; the keyed hash of the subscription; the
    encrypted JWT and when it was minted (J17); whether the project was read, and since when it has
    been unread; and the keys waiting then, each as HMAC-SHA-256 of AC73's key under
    `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`, first 32 hex characters (B4's fix), with when it was first sent, or
    "unsent since <t>" with, from draft 9, when it first failed with try-later or an unnamed answer
    (AC76's give-up clock); for each job candidate (J16), the keyed hash of its key and head with
    when a run first saw that head, and, if any, when a run first read one of rule (b)'s retried
    reasons for it, as that asks-merge run's `run_started_at` (draft 4, review round 3, N4; draft 5,
    N3); for each open question whose answer's pull request a run has seen open (AC77, J20), or
    found closed unmerged by AC77's closed read (draft 7), its keyed hash with when a run first saw
    it and, from draft 9, that pull request's number, encrypted as the JWT is (build review round 1,
    Sec 1; AC77's single read), kept while the question stays open, so that when that pull request
    closes unmerged the question waits at once, its session hold over, with one notification (AC77's
    "open again"; draft 6); and the usage part (J21, AC78), encrypted as the JWT is: the UTC year
    and month, the last step notified, a cost notification not yet sent, when the usage was last
    read and since when it has been unread. A state with no usage part is the usual start for AC78's
    steps (AC78). From stage 1b, rule 0's part (J16), sealed as the JWT is: each verdict the sender
    read, by the keyed hash of its blob sha, with its word (PASS, FAIL or neither, as `verdictOf`
    reads it), kept while an open pull request's file list still holds that blob; and, for each
    head `ownerCheckHeads` chooses (J16), the keyed hash of its key and head with the owner check's
    ETag and its last answer (its state, and whether its description starts `Owner: after agents`), kept while
    that head is open. These entries count toward the 5,000 with the others. No title, path,
    number, endpoint, key or usage figure in clear.
  - **New** means a key in this run's set and not in the last state (C). Sent keys are kept while
    they wait; a key that leaves the set is dropped, so it is new again if it returns. A project
    not read this run keeps its last keys.
  - **No state and an unreadable state are different** (N7's fix): the artifact list or download
    failing, or a forged state, is "unreadable": the run sends nothing and uploads nothing (AC76).
    Only when the list answers and holds no artifact the lookup takes (the first run, or none for 7
    days; draft 6: one it passes over counts as none) is it "no state", and then the run sends one summary, titled with the project's name, "Notifications are
    on: <n> things wait on you now" ("1 thing waits on you now" for one, "nothing waits on you
    now" for none; draft 6), opening Home, and records every key as sent (C).
  - **Duplicates:** a run that dies after sending and before its upload means the next run sends
    those keys again; the `Topic` and `tag` replace rather than add where the first is still
    waiting or showing (J17). A known limit, rare.
  - **The lookup's cost, and a rotated state key** (draft 9, build review round 1, Sec 7; known
    limits): the lookup lists the artifacts of each of its own successful runs that has none, one
    request each, up to the page's 100. Unreadable, budget-stopped and test runs upload nothing, so
    a long outage can cost up to about 100 requests a run. And after 100 such runs the last saved
    state falls off the page: a forged state then becomes "no state", and the sender starts afresh
    with its start-up summary. That is also what happens when the owner changes
    `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`: the last state no longer verifies, so the sender reads it as forged,
    sends nothing and keeps the "could not be trusted" issue open for about 100 of its runs (about 8
    hours of 5-minute checks, less with events), then starts afresh.
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J18` covers it with a fake artifact store: new keys against the
    last state; a project not read keeping its keys; a key leaving and returning; the bootstrap
    summary; "unreadable" for a failed list, a failed download, a forged HMAC and an oversized
    artifact, each sending nothing; an artifact from another workflow, from a branch and from
    another repository each passed over, never read (draft 6): with the sender's own older state
    on the page, that state is taken; with none, "no state"; a valid state on the second page not
    looked for; a listing whose newest 150 runs were
    skipped still finding the last good state, since only `success` runs are listed; a job
    candidate's head and retried reason kept across runs; the usage part unreadable without the
    key; the subscription's
    hash changing; and that no key can be matched to its item without `DESK_NOTIFY_STATE_KEY`
    (hashing every made-up key with a wrong key finds none); and (draft 7, Critic round 5, note
    11) the `recorded` part kept across runs, a found end from the closed read kept, an entry
    dropped when its question leaves (answered or gone), and recorded questions counted with the
    keys and job candidates toward the 5,000, a state over it not used; and (draft 9) a recorded
    entry's pull request number sealed, never in clear, and a state written under one key read
    under another taken as forged until its run leaves the page; and (stage 1b) rule 0's part kept
    across runs, sealed, a verdict dropped when no open file list holds its blob, a head's entry
    dropped when the head moves or the pull request closes, and its entries counted toward the
    5,000.

- **J19 — The desk page → a push subscription → the owner's GitHub secrets (added 2026-10-18,
  AC75).**
  - **The public key:** J7's `push.vapidPublicKey`, the 65-byte uncompressed P-256 public key as
    base64url with no padding, 87 characters (Setup N1). It is public, so it is committed in J7,
    not a secret.
  - **Subscribing** (C): on the tap only (W4). If `window.pushManager` exists (Declarative Web
    Push, iOS 18.4 and later, D1, single page B), `window.pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly:
    true, applicationServerKey})`, with no service worker; else
    `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js', {scope: '/'})`, then that registration's
    `pushManager.subscribe` with the same options (W6, W9, W12). A failure shows its words: "The
    desk couldn't turn notifications on: <the browser's reason>", with EXP-006's fallback named
    when the reason is the service worker's script.
  - **The value:** `JSON.stringify(subscription)` (V2), shown in a box the owner can select, with
    "Copy", and again from `getSubscription()` on "Show the value again". It is kept by the browser
    only; the desk stores nothing else and sends it nowhere. The owner puts the same value in both
    projects' `notify` Environments (Setup N6), since one phone receives both.
  - **A new subscription** (a new phone, the desk removed from the Home Screen and added again,
    `pushsubscriptionchange`, or the address changing at launch, Setup N10) means a new value: the
    owner updates the secret in both projects (N6). AC76's issue says so when the old one is gone.
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J19` covers it with a faked `window.pushManager`,
    `navigator.serviceWorker` and `Notification`: the key's decoding to 65 bytes starting `0x04`;
    each path; the value's form, matching what J17's first step accepts (the same parser, run on
    the page's output); and the failure words.

- **J20 — Open pull requests' files → "Your answer is being recorded" and the job candidates
  (desk page and senders; added 2026-10-18, draft 3, AC77, J16).**
  - **What is read:** for each open, non-draft pull request in J1's list into the default branch
    whose head is in the project's own repository (draft 6: only these can record an answer, AC77,
    or wait as a pull request and so matter as a job candidate, Terms; no other is read), its
    changed files, `GET /repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>/files` (at most 3 pages of 100), with `filename` and
    `status` (`added`, `removed`, `modified`, `renamed` with
    `previous_filename`, split as asks-merge splits it). A pull request from a fork is read for
    nothing more: it is never a job candidate and never records an answer.
  - **Its size** (review N5): one request per page, usually one (a pull request with up to 100
    files), at most three; each page counts 1 of the blob call's budget of 25, as a blob does (C).
  - **On the page** (C): the read travels in J6's blob call, as J12's query does: one to three
    requests per open pull request, made again only when its head sha changes, its answer kept by head sha in
    the page's memory. Service-Desk usually has none to three open (E), so a few requests a day.
    It is optional, like J11's reads: a failure leaves the question as an ordinary waiting one,
    with its link, and never touches "read successfully". For AC77's closed read, a failed file
    read of a closed pull request keeps the hold instead (draft 7; AC77).
  - **In a sender:** a REST read with the workflow's token, each run (J16).
  - **What it gives:** an open question `<name>` whose answer `decisions/questions/<name>.md` an
    open, non-draft pull request adds (v3), or whose file it deletes (v2.5 only; in v3 a deletion
    alone, such as a withdrawal, is not an answer, review round 3, N9), is **being recorded**
    (AC77); J16's job candidates; and, from 2026-10-19, the board's (AC80, J22): each pull request's
    changed files, for its risk class, and which `reviews/<n>/<id>.md` verdict files are on its
    branch, each with its blob `sha`, which J20 keeps for those files only, for J22's reads of the
    verdicts (the owner's, rule 1; from 2026-10-20 each required reviewer's, rule 0), and, in a
    sender, for J16's rule 0 reads by the same sha.
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J20` covers it with REST answers recorded once from
    Service-Desk's pull requests (as J12's fixture is) and made-up ones: an added answer record; a
    renamed file split in two; a deleted question file (v2.5, poom/'s placeholder form) read as
    being recorded, and the same deletion alone in a v3 project not; a fork's
    pull request ignored; a head change reading again, an
    unchanged head not; three pages; and a failed read leaving the question ordinary.

- **J21 — GitHub's billing usage → the desk's function and Service-Desk's sender (added
  2026-10-18, draft 4, AC78; draft 5 after research Q-015's source check, FAIL on F1.5 only,
  research/Q-015-source-check.md, CS19).**
  - **Who reads, and why both** (C, weighed as asked):
    - **the sender** (Workflow 3, Service-Desk's only) reads it for the $50 notifications, which
      must come when the desk is closed. Its runs are free, as a public repository's, and run at
      least every 5 minutes, so an hourly read costs nothing. Workflow 4 never reads it: its
      minutes are charged, and one reader is enough for one account;
    - **the desk's function** reads it for the bar. The sender's state is a public artifact in
      Service-Desk, so the figures may not sit there in clear (AC76); for the desk to read them
      from it, the function would need a second key shared with the sender, an artifact download
      and a zip to unpack, more parts than one read with a token held as a secret;
    - **not the page itself:** a read from the browser would put a billing token in the page, and
      whether GitHub's CORS preflight lets `X-GitHub-Api-Version` through is unknown (Q-015 F6.1,
      U-5). Both reads are server side; no figure passes between them, and both use the same
      reader in `src/lib/` (C), so they agree.
  - **The token** (Setup N12; the owner's, by hand; no agent holds it): one fine-grained personal
    access token of the account, repository access "Public repositories (read-only)", account
    permission Plan: Read-only and nothing else, with an expiry the owner chooses. Whether such a
    token works is a documented conflict, nothing more (Q-015's source check, F2.1 and F2.2: both
    first-party, unresolved): GitHub's REST data marks these endpoints for fine-grained tokens with
    Plan: read; its tutorial and its migration page say they do not take fine-grained tokens.
    UNKNOWN (U-1), so EXP-006 case 11 tries it once. Fallback, on 401, 403 or 404 (a 404 can be
    GitHub's answer to a token kind it does not take; review round 4, N7): a classic token, whose
    required scope is not documented (U-2): the owner tries no scope, then `read:user`, then
    `user`, keeps the first that answers 200 with Actions items, and records which; if none does,
    GitHub does not report Actions use for the account (U-11; AC78's "Not reported");
    Risks states a classic token's wider reach. The workflow's own token cannot call these
    endpoints (F2.4, A), and the desk's read token is not widened. It is set twice, with the same
    value: `DESK_BILLING_TOKEN` in Service-Desk's `notify` Environment, and the Pages secret
    `GITHUB_BILLING_TOKEN` (Production) on the preview, and on `needs-you` at launch (C6).
  - **The reads** (fixed in the code; the page sends no address, account or month), each with
    `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and
    `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`, `<y>` and `<m>` taken once per read from the UTC date:
    1. `GET /users/<account>/settings/billing/usage/summary?year=<y>&month=<m>&product=Actions`
       (Q-015 F1.2): its `usageItems`, for the estimate. GitHub's REST usage page says user
       endpoints "are only applicable if the user has purchased their own Copilot plan" (Q-015's
       source check, F1.5), so for this account it may hold no Actions items (U-11, AC78);
    2. `GET /users/<account>/settings/billing/usage?year=<y>&month=<m>` (F1.1): its `usageItems`,
       for the minutes by repository, and the estimate when the summary does not answer in form;
    3. `GET /users/<account>/repos?type=owner&per_page=100`, at most 3 pages: the account's public
       repositories (a user's repositories listed by name show only public ones; C), matched
       against `repositoryName` as `<account>/<name>` or `<name>`, since its form is not
       documented (EXP-006 case 11 records it).
  - **What is kept from them:** each item's `product`, `sku`, `unitType`, `quantity` or
    `netQuantity`, `pricePerUnit`, `netAmount` and `repositoryName`, and the public repositories'
    names; AC78 computes from these alone. Anything else is dropped.
  - **On the page** (C): an optional read riding J6's blob call, as J12's query does, made per
    opening: once when the desk opens, at most once an hour while that opening stays open, and
    again on a cost notification's tap, kept in the page's memory only (AC78), using 3 to 5 of the
    call's budget of 25. None is made while J7's `actionsUsage.reported` is `false`. The function answers `{"state": "ok" | "not-configured" | "refused" |
    "not-found" | "unavailable", "asOf": "<UTC>", ...}` with the kept fields only, never the
    token. It never touches "read successfully", the counts or "Quiet".
  - **In the sender:** only for the project whose J7 entry holds `actionsUsage` (draft 9, build
    review round 1, Sec 5), in a run whose J18 usage part shows the last read 60 minutes ago or
    more, with `DESK_BILLING_TOKEN` passed through `env:` to the one step that sends. Its requests
    count against the owner's own hourly limit, not the workflow token's, so J16's budget guard is
    not touched.
  - **The owner's limit:** a user's tokens share one hourly limit (C), with the desk's read token
    among them: at most 5 requests an hour from the sender, and 5 for each opening plus 5 an hour
    while it stays open, a few dozen a day (A3).
  - **Awkward cases:** an empty `usageItems`: 0 minutes and $0.00 on the month's 1st (UTC), and
    "Not reported" on any later day (AC78); the
    month turning during a read: the year and month taken once; the summary answering in another
    form: `/usage` used (AC78); `repositoryName` missing: counted (AC78); figures lagging by an
    unknown time (U-3): "as of", never "now"; the old `/settings/billing/actions` endpoint never
    called (F1.7, F1.8).
  - A test marked `join-test: S-001/J21` covers it with made-up answers in the documented form
    (NOT real, labelled so; no real billing figure enters this public repository): the three
    requests' fixed form; each state from 200, 401, 403, 404, 5xx and a body in another form; a
    200 with no Actions item (AC78's "Not reported", and 0% on the 1st); no read while `reported`
    is `false`; the page's reads per opening; the
    same reader giving the same figures on the page and in the sender; the kept fields only in the
    function's answer, and the token in no answer or log line; public repositories matched in both
    name forms; three pages of repositories; the at-most-hourly reads on both sides; and the read
    leaving "read successfully" and "Quiet" unchanged.

- **J22 — A pull request's risk class, its verdict file and GitHub's owner check → the board's step
  (desk page; added 2026-10-19, AC80; drafts 2 and 3).**
  - **What decides the step** (C, in this order, the first that applies):
    0. **with the agents** (from 2026-10-20; P-001-board-after-agents.md and
       P-001-domain-review-count.md, both A): the pull request is no card but counts in "With the
       agents" (AC80) while either holds:
       - (i) its owner check reads `pending` with a description starting `Owner: after agents`
         (owner_signal.py:167-179), in a project whose checks the page reads (below); or
       - (ii) a reviewer its change requires, other than the owner, has no verdict file at its head,
         or one that reads `Verdict: FAIL` or neither PASS nor FAIL. The change's required reviewers
         are its class's `[reviews]` list and every matching `[paths."<glob>"]` table's `reviews`,
         worked out from the same files and rules as (a)'s class below
         (governance/checks/review_check.py:317-346); each such `<id>` but `owner` needs
         `reviews/<n>/<id>.md` at the current head: in J20's list there, added or modified, or, when
         the list doesn't name it, in the default branch's tree J1 already reads (review_check reads
         the checked-out tree, which holds the default branch's files too; draft 3, the plan
         review's note 8, round 2), unless the list shows it `removed`. At 87ce4f0 every R1, R2 or
         R3 change needs `reviewer`, and one touching `src/public/**` needs `design-reviewer` too
         (governance/risk-paths.toml:33-35, :47-48).

       **How a verdict file is read** (draft 3; the plan review's B1, round 2): every verdict file,
       here and in rule 1, the sender's too (J16), is decided by the desk's own reader, `verdictOf`
       (src/lib/j11.js:56-74), which AC60 already uses and which decides as review_check's
       `parse_verdict` does (governance/checks/review_check.py:67-87): one leading byte-order mark
       dropped, lines split on LF with one trailing CR dropped, a `Verdict:` anywhere but a line's
       start making the file malformed, and the first `Verdict:` line deciding, `Verdict: PASS` or
       `Verdict: FAIL` followed only by spaces or tabs. Its `'PASS'` and `'FAIL'` are PASS and FAIL;
       its `'other'` (malformed) and `null` (no `Verdict:` line) are "neither". So `Verdict: PASS `
       with a trailing space, a Windows line ending or a leading byte-order mark reads PASS on the
       desk as it does in the governance check, never "neither", which would keep a pull request
       that needs the owner in "With the agents" (V1). A file in J20's list is read by the blob
       `sha` the list gives it; one only in the default branch's tree is the tree's own blob, read
       with the tree's other blobs where J11 already reads it (a v3 project's `reviews/<n>/` files,
       AC60), and otherwise not read, so counting as given (below): no read is added for it.

       A verdict file on the branch, or in the default branch's tree, whose blob is not read yet
       counts as given, until its read says otherwise (C: the safe side, so a pull request that
       needs the owner is never hidden, V1).
       **Rule 0 is never kept across heads** (draft 2; the plan review's note 1, round 1): it is
       judged afresh at each head from that head's reads, and the last head's judgement that rules 1
       to 7 keep (rule 7, AC80) is never rule 0's. A pull request whose files J20 has not read at its
       current head, at the first head the page has seen or at a later one (a read that failed, or
       one not made yet), a fork's, one with a list of 300 files or more, and every pull request of a
       project whose `governance/risk-paths.toml` is missing or can't be read, is judged by (i)
       alone. So a read failing just after the verdict commit that ends rule 0 shows the card at
       once, never hides it past 5 minutes. J20's read of a new head is optional: it is made only
       once the cycle's needed reads are in, and the optional loop stops at its first failed call
       (src/lib/scheduler.js:756-770, :790-794), so a new head can go unread for a cycle when its
       own read fails, when the cycle's needed reads fail or fill the cap, or when an earlier
       optional call fails; in each such cycle the pull request is judged by (i) alone, a brief
       card that need not be one, never a hidden one (draft 3; the plan review's note 3, round 2,
       which found draft 2's "only when that read fails" too narrow). Its fold's words:
       "Waiting on <the reviewer, in the roster's words>'s verdict", "<reviewer> asked for changes",
       "<reviewer>'s verdict reads neither PASS nor FAIL", or, for (i), "The agents still have
       findings to fix first." **One verdict call per head** (draft 2; the plan review's note 3,
       round 1): each head's verdict blobs, the owner's and every required reviewer's, ride together
       in one blob call of that head's own and nothing else, read once per blob sha in an opening:
       since a failed blob fails its whole call (src/lib/github.js:626-633), a failing one costs only
       that head's verdict reads that cycle, never the project's read, another head's verdicts or
       another read's answer, and each is asked again at rule 1's retry, inside the head's 5-poll
       bound. **These calls are not the optional loop's** (draft 3; the plan review's note 3, round
       2): that loop stops at its first failed call (src/lib/scheduler.js:790-794), so a head's
       verdict call riding it would stop every later head's. Each cycle makes them after the blob
       phase (`blobPhase`), **only when it returned `ok`** (draft 4; the plan review's note 6,
       round 3): when it failed or is still pending (`{ ok: false, pending: true }`, its needed reads
       not all in, src/lib/scheduler.js:770), they are skipped that cycle, each head's unread
       verdicts counting as given (above: a card, never a hidden one), and made at the next cycle
       whose blob phase returns `ok`; a skipped call is not a failed one, so it uses none of the
       head's 5 polls and adds no call to A3's count. They are made one head at a time in AC52's
       order, each its own call outside
       `MAX_BLOB_CALLS_PER_CYCLE`, as A3 counts them; a failed one is noted for its retry and the
       next head's call is still made; only a rate limit or a 401 stops the rest (as
       src/lib/github.js:673-676 does for a call). The page's stored cache keeps only blobs in the tree (src/lib/scheduler.js:415-427), so
       each head's verdict call is made again at each opening; A3 counts it per head. When neither
       (i) nor (ii) holds, rules 1 to 7 decide the step. The same rule, as a pure function, is the
       sender's (J16);
    1. **its verdict is on its branch:** J20's list at its current head holds
       `reviews/<n>/owner.md`, added or modified. The page reads that file's blob by the `sha` J20's
       list gives it (J20 keeps the `sha` for the verdict files only), once per blob sha, as an
       **optional read in the head's one verdict call** (rule 0's, above), with the required
       reviewers' verdict blobs and nothing else, so one failing branch blob never fails the
       project's read, another head's verdicts or another read's answer (draft 4, the
       Orchestrator's ruling on plan review note 4, kept; draft 3 of this amendment, the Critic's
       note 10, round 2, which found draft 2 still saying "alone"); a failed read is asked again only
       at J20's 5-minute wait (`FILES_RETRY_MS`), inside the head's 5-poll bound (AC80). **Meanwhile**, while the file
       is in J20's list but its blob is unread or its read failed, the card is "Open ↗" with "Your
       verdict is on GitHub; reading it…", never "Verdict ↗" again (GitHub's new-file page would
       refuse a file that exists). Read, it is decided by `verdictOf` (rule 0's "How a verdict file
       is read", reviews/README.md's rule as review_check reads it): `Verdict: PASS` gives the merge, "Step 2 of 2: merge" when
       (a) or (b) below held; `Verdict: FAIL` gives "Open ↗" with "You asked for changes"; and a
       file that reads neither gives "Open ↗" with "Your verdict file reads neither PASS nor FAIL"
       (C). The owner check reading `Owner requested changes` gives "Open ↗" with "You asked for
       changes" too, and `Owner approved` the merge, whatever the file's read state;
    2. **(a) its files need the owner's verdict,** by class or by a path-only flag: "Verdict ↗";
       - **by class:** each changed file (J20's list at its current head; both names of a renamed
         file) takes the highest class any rule in the project's own `governance/risk-paths.toml`
         gives it, or the file's `unmatched` class when none does; a `[paths."<glob>"]` domain table
         whose glob matches the path raises it to that table's `risk`. The change takes the highest
         class of its paths, and needs the owner's verdict when that class's `[reviews]` list holds
         `owner`, or a matching domain table's `reviews` does. This mirrors the model's own rule
         (governance/checks/govlib.py, `path_class`, `change_class` and `required`, :1003-1035),
         with its glob rules (:285-325): `**/` matches any leading directories, a trailing `dir/**`
         matches that directory and everything below it, `*` and `?` never cross `/`, and the rest
         is literal. At 304144d, Service-Desk's R3 paths need it (`R3 = ["reviewer", "owner"]`) and
         no other class does;
       - **by the two flags that need only paths** (the Orchestrator's ruling on plan review A): a
         dependency manifest the pull request adds, changes or deletes, both names of a renamed one
         included (review_check.py:265, :284-285), matched as the model's `is_manifest` matches it
         (a pattern without `/` matches the file's name at any depth,
         governance/checks/govlib.py:997-1002), against `[dependencies] manifests` or the model's
         defaults (`requirements*.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`,
         `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, :975-977); and a `[tests]` path (its `globs`, or the defaults
         `tests/**`, `**/*_test.py`, `**/test_*.py`, `**/*.test.js`, `**/*.spec.ts`, :968-969) that
         the pull request deletes or renames away, which the model counts as deleted
         (`--no-renames`, governance/checks/review_check.py:156-162, :188-192). The flags that need
         a file's contents (a skip marker, fewer assertions, a broad catch) are (b)'s to see;
    3. **(b) GitHub's owner check asks for it:** the `owner-verdict` commit status at its head reads
       state `pending` with a description starting `Owner verdict needed`
       (governance/checks/owner_signal.py, `verdict_status`, :148-182; model S-004): "Verdict ↗";
    4. **the owner check can't say:** state `error` (among them its tripwire's "CI code changed ·
       check the PR", which the owner-signal job posts in place of its verdict whenever a pull
       request changes a signal-code path, by default `.github/**`, `tools/**`, `tests/**`,
       `scripts/**`, `governance/checks/**` and `src/**`, governance/checks/govlib.py:981,
       owner_signal.py:204-218) (from 2026-10-20 `pending` with "Owner: after agents · …",
       :167-179, is rule 0's): "Open ↗",
       with "GitHub flagged a change to this project's code or checks: look at the changes, then
       merge or add your verdict." for the tripwire, and "GitHub's owner check couldn't decide." for
       any other `error`, each
       with the check's own description under it. Such a status can hide a needed verdict as well as
       a needless one, so it is never read as "no verdict" (the Orchestrator's ruling on plan review
       A). **This is the usual card for a Service-Desk code change today** (Critic L and plan review
       K, round 2): the default signal-code paths take in `src/**` and `tests/**`, and
       Service-Desk's `governance/risk-paths.toml` doesn't narrow them, so nearly every Builder pull
       request gets the tripwire's `error`, unless its verdict file already decides it (rule 1).
       **Why rule 4 and rule 6 differ:** in rule 4 GitHub's check was posted and asks the owner to
       look at the pull request, so the card passes that on; in rule 6 there is no such request,
       only no answer, so the card goes by the files and says so ("By its files, …"). **If the
       project later narrows `signal_code`** (a separate governance change the Chief of Staff may
       propose, outside this spec), most of these cards become "Merge ↗" or "Verdict ↗" by rules 3
       and 5, with no change to this spec;
    5. **"Owner not required":** "Merge ↗", "It needs no verdict from you, only the merge.";
    6. **not read:** (a) found no need and the owner check is not read (not yet posted, past the
       3-head cap, a failed read, or a project whose checks the page doesn't read, below): "Merge
       ↗", with "By its files, it needs no verdict from you, only the merge; GitHub's owner check:
       not read yet." (C);
    7. **not known:** (a) can't be judged (J20's list failed or not yet read at the first head the
       page has seen, a fork's pull request, for which J20 reads nothing, a list of 300 files or
       more, or `governance/risk-paths.toml` missing or not readable) and nothing above applies:
       "Open ↗", "Whether it needs your verdict: not known yet". After a head change the card keeps
       the last head's judgement until J20 has read the new one (AC80); rule 0's is never kept
       (above).
  - **The file's read:** `governance/risk-paths.toml` on the default branch, for every connected
    project, v3 or v2.5 (registered with the optional reads outside J11's v3-only block,
    src/lib/model.js), as one optional blob, read again only when its blob sha changes (A3). The
    page reads only the part of TOML the file uses: `key = "string"`, `key = [ "string", … ]` over
    one or more lines, and comments after `#` outside a string; of its keys, `unmatched`,
    `[classes]`, `[reviews]`, `[paths."<glob>"]` (`risk` and `reviews`), `[tests] globs` and
    `[dependencies] manifests`, each taking the model's default when absent; every other key or
    table (`signal_code`, `[tests]`'s other keys, a domain's `checks`) is skipped
    (governance/checks/govlib.py:963-990, :1068-1070). A file it can't read is "not known" for (a),
    never a class.
  - **The owner check's read** (J1, J6): `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status?per_page=100`,
    GitHub's combined status, as a conditional request with the page's ETag, in the poll call,
    **only for a v3 project whose repository is public** (the Orchestrator's ruling on plan review
    I): J1's open-pull-request list gives `base.repo.private` on every pull request, and the page
    sends the part only when it reads `false`. So Personal-Org-Operating-Model (v2.5 and private)
    gets none. **A head not read** (C; stage 1a's build review, round 1, finding 4): the function
    answers `false` alike for a 403, a 5xx, a network failure and a malformed part (J6), so the page
    can't tell a refusal from a passing failure and treats every `false` alike: that head's check is
    "not read" (rules 0 to 6 below), and it is asked again in the poll call of the first poll at
    least 5 minutes later (`FILES_RETRY_MS`, J20's wait), not sooner, and not left unasked for the
    rest of the opening; a 200 or a 304 ends the wait. The retry rides a poll call made anyway, so
    it adds no function call (A3 unchanged) and stays inside J1's 30 requests (11 + 3 + 16); a
    head refused all day costs at most 12 GitHub requests an hour on each open device. Such a head
    keeps its place among the 3: its place never passes to a fourth head, so the page and the
    sender, which share `ownerCheckHeads` (the sender knows nothing of the page's failures), still
    choose the same heads (J16). At most 3 heads a project (C),
    chosen by `ownerCheckHeads` in the shared module, the same function the sender uses, so both
    read the check for the same heads (J16; draft 3, the plan review's note 4, round 2). **Which
    heads** (draft 4; the Critic's B1 and the plan review's note 5, round 3): the open pull
    requests of the project, from the verdicts and lists read so far, leaving out only one settled
    by its owner's verdict file (J20's list at its head holds `reviews/<n>/owner.md`, added or
    modified, and `verdictOf` reads it PASS or FAIL, rule 1, so GitHub's check no longer says
    "Owner: after agents") and one already with the agents by (ii), for which (i) would change
    nothing; whatever (a) gives. So a pull request (a) marks, the owner-required ones by class or
    path,
    where GitHub posts "Owner: after agents" (owner_signal.py:163-179, which gives "Owner not
    required" to every other change), is read too, once its reviewers' verdicts are in; draft 3
    left out every such pull request (the open pull requests "whose card is not already "Verdict
    ↗" by (a)"), so (i) could hold almost only where (b) applies, and the ruling's case went
    unread. A pull request whose J20 list is not read at its current head (a failed or pending
    read, a fork's, one of 300 files or more), or whose project's `governance/risk-paths.toml`
    can't be read, can be neither left out by these rules nor judged but by (i) (rule 0), so it is
    chosen like any other. They are taken in AC52's order (`created_at`, oldest first), two with the
    same `created_at` by the lower number first, so the page and the sender, whose lists may come
    in different orders, choose alike, and the first 3 are read. The bound stays 3 a project, as
    J1's 30 requests a poll call need (11 + 3 + 16), so A3's count is unchanged. The page takes the
    `owner-verdict` entry's `state` and `description`. A 304 costs no GitHub rate (Facts relied
    on). A fourth such pull request is judged without it ("not read"). A failed, refused or
    malformed answer is "not read", never "not required".
  - **A known limit:** where the owner check is not read (a private or v2.5 project, or a fourth
    head), a need only a file's contents give (a weakened test) is not seen, and the card shows
    "Merge ↗" with "By its files, …", so the owner knows the check was not read; GitHub's own page
    shows that check. **And (i) can't hold for a change that trips the tripwire** (draft 4; the
    Critic's B1, round 3): for a pull request that changes a signal-code path, the owner-signal job
    posts `error` "CI code changed · check the PR" in place of its verdict
    (governance/checks/owner_signal.py:211-213), never "Owner: after agents". At Service-Desk that
    is nearly every Builder pull request (rule 4). Once its required reviewers' verdicts are in,
    such a pull request still waiting on the agents' fixes is a card (rule 2 or rule 4: "Verdict ↗"
    where (a) marks it, as it does the R3 signal-code paths, else "Open ↗"; the confirmation check
    of draft 4, N1), and the sender notifies for it: a needless card, never a hidden one, and only
    (ii) puts it with the agents. The limit is the model's check, not the desk's; it narrows only
    if the project narrows `signal_code` (rule 4). The lead tells the owner. **And a later head is
    pushed to fourth more often** (the confirmation check of draft 4, N2): since the pull requests
    (a) marks take the 3 places too, among them ones that trip the tripwire, for which the read
    changes nothing (`error` never gives (i), and rule 2 comes before rules 3 and 4), a later head
    is left fourth, "not read", more often than in draft 3. There a need only (b) gives shows rule
    6's "Merge ↗" with "not read yet", and an R3 pull request outside the signal-code paths misses
    (i), so it is a card while the agents fix it: a needless card, never a hidden one, and no call
    is added. The lead tells the owner. And a future private v3 project would rely on the page's
    `base.repo.private` alone, since the function's own check (`"ownerChecks": null` for a non-v3
    project) looks only at the model (plan review I, round 3).
